articles.title: Congress proposes four-point formula for delimitation, says INDIA bloc on board
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Party proposes retaining 543 Lok Sabha seats, existing State-wise distribution and a 25-year freeze, with one-third reservation for women

The Congress party on Friday said it favoured resolving the issue of delimitation through consultations with all political parties, but accused the government of making no effort to engage the Opposition on the matter.

Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh said the party’s position was guided by a four-point formula: retaining the existing strength of 543 seats in the Lok Sabha; maintaining the present State-wise distribution of seats; reserving one-third (182) of the existing seats for women; and imposing a 25-year freeze on all three arrangements.

Mr. Ramesh said the need for an early consensus on the issue had become more pressing in view of of the fact that Article 82 of the Constitution will come into force and delimitation would be held once the results of the ongoing Census exercise are out early next year.
This could be unfavourable to some southern states – which have made progress in population control – and hence not feasible, he added.
Mr. Ramesh said the Congress was not opposed to delimitation as such, but believed that the exercise should not place any State at a disadvantage.

The Congress leader claimed that all parties in the INDIA bloc, including the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) and the Nationalist Congress Party (Sharadchandra Pawar), were on the same page on the four-point formula.
The DMK, he said, was also party to a resolution opposing any change in the number of Lok Sabha seats and seeking safeguards to ensure that Tamil Nadu was not disadvantaged by delimitation.
The Congress leader said seeking consultation was necessary because the government had not initiated any meaningful engagement with the Opposition.
He claimed that as per his information, the government has not shared a concrete proposal on delimitation even with constituents of the National Democratic Alliance.
The Congress wanted the matter to be discussed with all political parties and stakeholders to arrive at a consensus, Mr. Ramesh added.

articles.title: Patna High Court quashes dismissal of teachers and staff of Sanskrit Colleges
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The court has directed the Bihar Education Department to release the grant-in-aid to the university within three months.

Principals, teachers, and non-teaching staff of various Sanskrit colleges affiliated with Kameshwar Singh Darbhanga Sanskrit University (KSDSU) received relief from the Patna High Court on Friday (November 20, 2026).

A single-judge bench presided over by Justice Kumar Manish, while hearing 12 connected petitions (lead case: Birendra Prasad Thakur v. State of Bihar, CWJC No. 13475/2022), quashed all dismissal orders issued by the Director of Higher Education and the university.

The petitioners were appointed between 2008 and 2015 in various affiliated and “deficit grant-in-aid” Sanskrit colleges located in Supaul, West Champaran, East Champaran, Patna, Saran, and Jehanabad, following due process involving public advertisements and selection committees.

Despite the university’s Syndicate confirming their services, the Director of Higher Education cited the absence of prior approval from the State Government, as required under Section 35(2) of the Bihar State Universities Act, 1976, and rejected these appointments on April 21, 2022, and November 2, 2022. Subsequently, the university issued directives to terminate their services.

In its judgment, the High Court cited the ruling of a Full Bench in Braj Kishore Singh v. State of Bihar (1997). The Court clarified that, when posts have already been created and sanctioned (under an established ‘staffing pattern’) pursuant to the State Government’s resolution dated October 18, 1976, separate ‘prior approval’ from the government is not mandatory for appointments to those posts made through a valid selection process.
“Dismissing an employee on technical grounds after more than a decade of service constitutes a violation of Articles 14, 16, and 21 of the Constitution,” the court observed.
Expressing concern over the proliferation of unnecessary litigation in cases of a similar nature, the court cited Clause 4(C)(1) of the Bihar State Litigation Policy, 2011.
The court directed that a copy of the order be sent to the Chief Secretary and the Advocate General. The court emphasised that such similar cases should be resolved at the departmental level.

Declaring the service of all the petitioners to be valid, the court has directed the Bihar Education Department to release the grant-in-aid to the university within three months of receiving a copy of the order.
“This is to ensure that the petitioners receive their regular current salaries, as well as all outstanding salary arrears accrued from the date of their initial appointment,” the court said.

articles.title: Woman delivers triplets after non-ART treatment at Telangana govt. hospital; premature babies discharged after NICU care
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: After a nine-year wait and unsuccessful fertility treatment at private hospitals, a couple welcomed triplet boys following treatment at Gandhi Hospital’s IVF Centre. The premature babies, who weighed between 1.4 kg and 1.5 kg at birth, spent over a month in the hospital’s Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU). They were discharged along with their 32-year-old mother after responding well to treatment.
Avanthi enrolled at Gandhi Hospital’s IVF Centre in January this year. Doctors opted for ovulation induction, a non-assisted reproductive treatment, and she conceived in the second cycle.

articles.title: Anthropic researcher says Claude solved maths’ greatest riddle
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: First proposed by German mathematician Bernhard Riemann in 1859, the hypothesis concerns the distribution of prime numbers and is widely regarded as the most important open question in pure mathematics

A mathematician at AI company Anthropic said Friday (November 20, 2026) that he had used the firm’s Claude chatbot to prove the Riemann Hypothesis, a problem that has eluded mathematicians for more than 160 years.
“I believe I have, working with Claude, discovered proof of the Riemann Hypothesis,” Levent Alpoge wrote in a four-page note released Friday (November 20, 2026).
The claim has not been independently verified, and the proof has not yet been reviewed by outside experts.

First proposed by German mathematician Bernhard Riemann in 1859, the hypothesis concerns the distribution of prime numbers and is widely regarded as the most important open question in pure mathematics.
It is one of seven Millennium Prize Problems selected by the Clay Mathematics Institute in 2000, which offers $1 million for a solution to each.
Under the institute’s rules, a solution must be published in a peer-reviewed journal and withstand two years of scrutiny.
Mr. Alpoge said the method also resolves a broader version of the problem known as the Generalised Riemann Hypothesis.

He said he and Claude had produced a version of the proof in Lean, a programming language that allows mathematical arguments to be checked by a computer, and that he was releasing only that version for now.
A full written argument would be extremely long, he said, adding that he had not yet mastered all of the mathematics involved and planned to write it up properly.

Mr. Alpoge said he had consulted Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei before announcing the result and acknowledged that its timing could be viewed cynically, without elaborating, though he was probably referring to this week’s record IPO.

articles.title: Three to tango: On Trump, Xi, Putin trilateral summit
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: U.S., China, Russia must draw up a roadmap for talks on nuclear weapons

The first trilateral summit between the Presidents of China, the U.S. and Russia , held in Shenzhen on November 19, reflected both the changing global order and the leaders’ shared desire to remain engaged with one another in an increasingly unpredictable world. For U.S. President Donald Trump, the summit was a platform where he could push for joint talks between the world’s three largest nuclear powers on reducing nuclear warheads. After the New START treaty between the U.S. and Russia expired in February 2026, Moscow had signalled that it was ready for talks, but Mr. Trump wanted to involve China as well. For President Xi Jinping, the summit reinforced China’s position as a peer competitor to the U.S. While Russia seeks to deepen partnership with China, the U.S. is looking to build strategic stability. And for Russian President Vladimir Putin, whom the West sought to isolate after he launched the invasion of Ukraine, the summit offered a seat at the high table. The decision to start trilateral talks on nuclear arms and the joint declaration, which stated that ‘a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought’, are steps in the right direction. But much will depend on what follows.

Many had compared the meet to the 1945 Yalta Conference, when Russian leader Joseph Stalin, U.S. President Franklin D. Roosevelt and British Prime Minister Winston Churchill met to discuss the future of post-War Europe. But Shenzhen was not a summit of the victors of a major war. This was more about three great powers setting terms of engagement in a changing world. The summit failed to achieve any breakthrough on any of the issues on the agenda — nuclear arms reduction, non-proliferation or the Ukraine war — or even offer a road map for the future. Moreover, it is not clear if the Shenzhen spirit could be sustained in the medium to long-term as another President in the U.S. could take a very different approach towards Russia and China. The three leaders have called for reform of the UN. While it is a welcome move, any attempt to reform the international system and institutions must also involve other powers, particularly rising middle powers such as India, South Africa and Brazil. But the Shenzhen framework could bring greater stability and predictability to great-power relations. This is important given that two of the Big Three are currently waging two separate wars. The leaders should draw up a clear road map for nuclear talks and other key issues outlined in the Shenzhen declaration, with realistic and achievable objectives. Otherwise, the summit would amount to little more than another diplomatic photo-op.

📰 Three to tango: On Trump, Xi, Putin trilateral summit

U.S., China, Russia must draw up a roadmap for talks on nuclear weapons

The first trilateral summit between the Presidents of China, the U.S. and Russia , held in Shenzhen on November 19, reflected both the changing global order and the leaders’ shared desire to remain engaged with one another in an increasingly unpredictable world. For U.S. President Donald Trump, the summit was a platform where he could push for joint talks between the world’s three largest nuclear powers on reducing nuclear warheads. After the New START treaty between the U.S. and Russia expired in February 2026, Moscow had signalled that it was ready for talks, but Mr. Trump wanted to involve China as well. For President Xi Jinping, the summit reinforced China’s position as a peer competitor to the U.S. While Russia seeks to deepen partnership with China, the U.S. is looking to build strategic stability. And for Russian President Vladimir Putin, whom the West sought to isolate after he launched the invasion of Ukraine, the summit offered a seat at the high table. The decision to start trilateral talks on nuclear arms and the joint declaration, which stated that ‘a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought’, are steps in the right direction. But much will depend on what follows.

Many had compared the meet to the 1945 Yalta Conference, when Russian leader Joseph Stalin, U.S. President Franklin D. Roosevelt and British Prime Minister Winston Churchill met to discuss the future of post-War Europe. But Shenzhen was not a summit of the victors of a major war. This was more about three great powers setting terms of engagement in a changing world. The summit failed to achieve any breakthrough on any of the issues on the agenda — nuclear arms reduction, non-proliferation or the Ukraine war — or even offer a road map for the future. Moreover, it is not clear if the Shenzhen spirit could be sustained in the medium to long-term as another President in the U.S. could take a very different approach towards Russia and China. The three leaders have called for reform of the UN. While it is a welcome move, any attempt to reform the international system and institutions must also involve other powers, particularly rising middle powers such as India, South Africa and Brazil. But the Shenzhen framework could bring greater stability and predictability to great-power relations. This is important given that two of the Big Three are currently waging two separate wars. The leaders should draw up a clear road map for nuclear talks and other key issues outlined in the Shenzhen declaration, with realistic and achievable objectives. Otherwise, the summit would amount to little more than another diplomatic photo-op.

articles.title: BIADA allots 64.23 acres of land to 33 industrial units in Bihar
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Industrial units likely to bring in investment of ₹ 915.52 crore; Expected to generate approximately 2300 employment opportunities.
Bihar Industrial Area Development Authority (BIADA) has approved the allotment of 64.23 acres of land, along with Plug and Play sheds, to 33 new industrial units.
These projects are likely to bring in investment of approximately ₹915.52 crore. Besides, these units are expected to generate around 2,300 employment opportunities across the State.
The approvals were granted on Thursday (November 19, 2026) at the BIADA’s Project Clearance Committee (PCC) meeting chaired by its (BIADA’s) Managing Director Naveen Kumar.

BIADA, a State government agency under Industries department, develops industrial areas and allots land or sheds for industrial units across the State. It supports industrial growth, infrastructure, and investment incentives in the State.
The committee also approved the proposals for Plug & Play facilities to facilitate faster establishment and commencement of industrial operations.

These facilities will provide investors with ready-to-use industrial infrastructure, thereby reducing the time required to establish industrial units, facilitating the early commencement of production, and making it easier for entrepreneurs to conduct business.
The meeting also discussed various proposals concerning the allotment of industrial land and the establishment of new industrial units across the State.
The proposed projects span diverse sectors, including food processing, textiles, garment manufacturing, UPVC pipe manufacturing, PU foam, bags and general manufacturing.
These units are proposed to be set up across various industrial areas in the State, including Kumarbagh, Sikandarpur, Patliputra, Fatuha, Bariyarpur, IGC Aurangabad, Nawanagar, and Biharsharif.

With expanding industrial infrastructure, faster investment facilitation and new employment opportunities, Bihar is steadily strengthening its position as an emerging manufacturing and investment destination.

articles.title: Koti Deepotsavam emerges as grand confluence of Shaiva, Vaishnava traditions in Telangana
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Bringing together revered spiritual heads, sacred rituals and devotees from across the State, the annual celebration offers a rare opportunity to experience diverse Hindu traditions at one venue, with the illumination of a crore earthen lamps forming its grand spectacle

A confluence of Shaiva and Vaishnava traditions, a congregation of revered spiritual heads from across the country and the illumination of a crore lamps have made Koti Deepotsavam one of Telangana’s biggest religious celebrations outside temple premises.

Held every year in Kartika month, the event draws thousands of devotees from different parts of the State, not merely to witness the ceremonies but also to participate in an array of rituals that are otherwise not easily accessible to the common devotee.
Koti Deepotsavam offers devotees an opportunity to perform abhishekams, offer bilva leaves to Shiva Lingams, worship the Goddess and participate in special pujas and other ceremonies.
The presence of Jagadgurus and heads of prominent peethams adds another dimension, enabling devotees to seek their blessings and have their darshan, an opportunity that many may seldom get otherwise.

Over the past 13 years, Koti Deepotsavam has given a distinctive identity to the month of Kartika and to Telangana. The initiative began in 2012 as a Laksha Deepotsavam, or the lighting of one lakh lamps, and the following year evolved into Koti Deepotsavam, involving a crore lamps. The idea was conceived by Narendra Chowdary and his wife Ramadevi, and daughter Rachana, who run Bhakti TV.

The genesis of the initiative lay in a visit by Sringeri Dakshinamnaya Peetham Jagadguru Sri Bharati Tirtha Mahaswami to Hyderabad during his Vijaya Yatra in 2012, when Kartika Deepotsavam was combined with the darshan of the Jagadguru for the Guru Vandanam.

The first edition was organised at NTR Stadium, where a specially constructed stage depicting the grandeur of Kailasa provided the setting for the celebrations. The Sringeri Jagadguru performed Deeparadhana and blessed the devotees.

By 2013, the Laksha Deepotsavam had grown into Koti Deepotsavam. What began as a single religious gathering gradually developed into an elaborate annual celebration, incorporating several traditions, rituals and cultural presentations.
“The objective has been to recreate the experience of visiting important pilgrimage centres by bringing the deities and their traditions together at one venue,” says Mr. Narendra Chowdary.

A distinctive feature is the presence of utsava murtis representing important temples and pilgrimage centres. Deities associated with the 12 Jyotirlingas, Pancha Bhuta Lingas, 18 Shakti Peethas and Divya Desams of the Sri Vaishnava tradition are brought to the venue and worshipped. Shaiva centres such as Ujjain, Arunachalam, Vemulawada and Kaleshwaram find representation alongside Vaishnava shrines such as Yadadri and Srirangam, and Shakti Peethas including Alampur, Kanchi and Varanasi.

The first edition was organised at NTR Stadium, where a specially constructed stage depicting the grandeur of Kailasa provided the setting for the celebrations. The Sringeri Jagadguru performed Deeparadhana and blessed the devotees.

By 2013, the Laksha Deepotsavam had grown into Koti Deepotsavam. What began as a single religious gathering gradually developed into an elaborate annual celebration, incorporating several traditions, rituals and cultural presentations.

“The objective has been to recreate the experience of visiting important pilgrimage centres by bringing the deities and their traditions together at one venue,” says Mr. Narendra Chowdary.

A distinctive feature is the presence of utsava murtis representing important temples and pilgrimage centres. Deities associated with the 12 Jyotirlingas, Pancha Bhuta Lingas, 18 Shakti Peethas and Divya Desams of the Sri Vaishnava tradition are brought to the venue and worshipped. Shaiva centres such as Ujjain, Arunachalam, Vemulawada and Kaleshwaram find representation alongside Vaishnava shrines such as Yadadri and Srirangam, and Shakti Peethas including Alampur, Kanchi and Varanasi.

articles.title: India says no change in its position on Indus Water Treaty as Pakistan minister attends SCO forum in Delhi
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: India suspended the treaty in 2025 as one of the punitive measures against Pakistan after the April 22 Pahalgam terror attack last year that claimed 26 lives

India's position on the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) is "very clear" and there has been "absolutely no change" in it, the Ministry of External Affairs said on Friday (November 20, 2026), amid a visit by Pakistan Minister Musadik Malik to attend the SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum in Delhi.

Mr. Malik, who arrived here in the early hours of Friday (November 20, 2026), attended the opening day of the three-day forum in the evening. The event, being hosted by India at the historic Purana Quila, was inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
India had announced on October 28 that invitations had been extended to all SCO members, including Pakistan, in keeping with established practice.
It was perhaps the first time New Delhi had invited a Pakistani minister to attend an event in India since the May 7-10 military hostilities last year following Operation Sindoor.
Pakistan had announced on November 14 that its Climate Change Minister Malik would participate in the forum.
"As far as IWT is concerned, we have made our position very clear, and that is where it remains. There is absolutely no change," Mr. Jaiswal said.
India suspended the treaty in 2025 as one of the punitive measures against Pakistan after the April 22 Pahalgam terror attack last year that claimed 26 lives.
Mr. Malik's participation in the forum is being seen by some experts as an opportunity in a multilateral framework that may help improve ties between the two neighbours.

Interacting with reporters on the sidelines of the forum, Mr. Malik, when asked about the role of culture in fostering better ties between India and Pakistan, said, "Culture has a very key role to play".

Hours before the inauguration, the MEA on Friday (November 20, 2026) said the forum was a "multilateral event within the SCO framework", for which invitations had been extended to all members of the grouping, including Pakistan.

India's position on the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) is "very clear" and there has been "absolutely no change" in it, the Ministry of External Affairs said on Friday (November 20, 2026), amid a visit by Pakistan Minister Musadik Malik to attend the SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum in Delhi.

Mr. Malik, who arrived here in the early hours of Friday (November 20, 2026), attended the opening day of the three-day forum in the evening. The event, being hosted by India at the historic Purana Quila, was inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

India had announced on October 28 that invitations had been extended to all SCO members, including Pakistan, in keeping with established practice.

It was perhaps the first time New Delhi had invited a Pakistani minister to attend an event in India since the May 7-10 military hostilities last year following Operation Sindoor.

Pakistan had announced on November 14 that its Climate Change Minister Malik would participate in the forum.

"As far as IWT is concerned, we have made our position very clear, and that is where it remains. There is absolutely no change," Mr. Jaiswal said.

India suspended the treaty in 2025 as one of the punitive measures against Pakistan after the April 22 Pahalgam terror attack last year that claimed 26 lives.

Mr. Malik's participation in the forum is being seen by some experts as an opportunity in a multilateral framework that may help improve ties between the two neighbours.

Interacting with reporters on the sidelines of the forum, Mr. Malik, when asked about the role of culture in fostering better ties between India and Pakistan, said, "Culture has a very key role to play".

Hours before the inauguration, the MEA on Friday (November 20, 2026) said the forum was a "multilateral event within the SCO framework", for which invitations had been extended to all members of the grouping, including Pakistan.

articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: “In four days, I met more than 20 world leaders, secured two new trade deals, and about 10 others coming very soon,” Donald Trump told a press conference at the White House in Washington

U.S. President Donald Trump on Friday (November 20, 2026) said he secured two trade deals with Thailand and the Philippines during his visit to Manila, adding that around 10 more agreements were expected soon.
“In four days, I met more than 20 world leaders, secured two new trade deals, and about 10 others coming very soon,” Mr. Trump told a press conference at the White House in Washington.

Mr. Trump also referred to India's interest rates and the high economic growth it achieved.

“Look at India, they have low interest rates, and they have a seven per cent growth rate,” Mr. Trump said, adding that the U.S. could achieve economic growth in the range of 14-15% if it had lower interest rates.
Mr Trump also referred to his meeting with the leaders of the Quad, comprising the U.S., India, Japan, and Australia.

"We announced the first-ever Quad Bureau Leaders' Forum to cooperate on matters of economic security, we launched a Quad SI Accelerator, and we agreed to a new collaboration on maritime security and surveillance operations" Mr. Trump said.
India and the U.S. finalised the framework for the first phase of the trade agreement in February. However, changes in the tariff landscape have led to further negotiations on the agreement.
India is seeking lower tariffs on its goods in the U.S. market than its competitors such as Bangladesh, Vietnam, and Cambodia.

articles.title: Magnitude 6.9 earthquake shakes Peru’s Andes, with no damage or casualties immediately reported
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Peru's Geophysical Institute said no damage or casualties had been reported. The earthquake was felt in the Peruvian capital, prompting residents to rush into the streets
A magnitude 6.9 earthquake shook the Andes in central Peru on Friday (November 20, 2026) with no immediate reports of damage or casualties.

The U.S. Geological Survey said the earthquake struck at 7:09 pm local time (0900 GMT Saturday). Its epicentre was in the Andes, 34 kilometres (21 miles) north of Junin, at a depth of 108 kilometres (67 miles).
Peru's Geophysical Institute said no damage or casualties had been reported. The earthquake was felt in the Peruvian capital, prompting residents to rush into the streets.
Peru lies along the "Ring of Fire", a 40,000-kilometre (25,000-mile) arc of volcanoes and fault lines around the Pacific Basin, where most of the world's earthquakes occur.

In August, a 6.7 magnitude earthquake in the Peruvian Andes left two people injured and damaged several homes, health centres and schools, while in July, a 5.5-magnitude quake in the Junín region resulted in six deaths and 30 injuries.

articles.title: Incomplete remedies: On Special Summary Revision of electoral rolls
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: The ECI offers relief to a section of deleted electors but SIR’s flaws remain

Following the Special Summary Revision (SSR) by the Election Commission of India (ECI) in some States that had undergone the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) , mostly in Phases 1 and 2, some 74 lakh names were added onto the electoral rolls. This meant that the electorate in those 13 States, that had shrunk from 49.61 crore to 45.22 crore after the SIR, has now gone up to 45.96 crore. The ECI has extended the SSR to States and UTs in Phase 3. As before, it requires no proof of citizenship or mapping to older rolls, and insists on personal notice before any deletion other than of the dead. It also directs Electoral Registration Officers (EROs) to cross-verify deletions personally wherever they exceed 2% of a polling station’s electors. Draft deletions in Phase 3 of the SIR averaged 17% , and reached 32.8% in Delhi . The ECI also offered another opportunity to electors deleted by the SIR in the seven States and UTs where it is still underway, such as Delhi and Maharashtra, to return to the rolls. Electors who did not return their forms can do so now, explaining the delay, and those who moved within the State can return through the enumeration form with proof of their new address. EROs will process these forms under Rule 21(1) of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, and restore the elector’s old EPIC number.

These “corrective” measures follow the Supreme Court’s observation on October 28 that forcing deleted electors to re-enrol through Form 6, meant for new voters, was an “error”. The ECI’s use of remedies that existed in the registration rules is a tacit admission that it went wrong during the SIR. But the measures are limited. They reach roughly 4.5 crore of the 13.37 crore struck off the draft rolls and do not cover electors who moved out of their States. Electors in States where the SIR has concluded, including Bihar and West Bengal, which have already voted on the SIR rolls, can return only through the SSR, by filing Form 6 as new voters, with fresh EPIC numbers and no record that they were ever on the roll. In essence, the structure of the SIR remains intact. Electors must still provide details from “the last SIR”, and those whose details are unavailable or do not match will be asked for documents in a manner that amounts to a citizenship test. The legality of the ludicrous “logical discrepancy” checks remains unaddressed. The 2002-03 special revision offered a better way. Those who had shifted homes were enumerated door to door at their new addresses. The Supreme Court must direct the ECI to return to that model.

The ECI also offered another opportunity to electors deleted by the SIR in the seven States and UTs where it is still underway, such as Delhi and Maharashtra, to return to the rolls. Electors who did not return their forms can do so now, explaining the delay, and those who moved within the State can return through the enumeration form with proof of their new address. EROs will process these forms under Rule 21(1) of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, and restore the elector’s old EPIC number.
• These “corrective” measures follow the Supreme Court’s observation on October 28 that forcing deleted electors to re-enrol through Form 6, meant for new voters, was an “error”. The ECI’s use of remedies that existed in the registration rules is a tacit admission that it went wrong during the SIR. But the measures are limited. They reach roughly 4.5 crore of the 13.37 crore struck off the draft rolls and do not cover electors who moved out of their States. Electors in States where the SIR has concluded, including Bihar and West Bengal, which have already voted on the SIR rolls, can return only through the SSR, by filing Form 6 as new voters, with fresh EPIC numbers and no record that they were ever on the roll. In essence, the structure of the SIR remains intact. Electors must still provide details from “the last SIR”, and those whose details are unavailable or do not match will be asked for documents in a manner that amounts to a citizenship test. The legality of the ludicrous “logical discrepancy” checks remains unaddressed. The 2002-03 special revision offered a better way. Those who had shifted homes were enumerated door to door at their new addresses. The Supreme Court must direct the ECI to return to that model.

articles.title: Outlook outage: On Microsoft and dangers of centralising digital systems
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: The dangers of centralising the internet’s architecture are now clear

Last week, Microsoft’s suite of productivity and email software, which businesses, governments, hospitals and a host of other organisations rely upon round-the-clock, abruptly stopped working globally , affecting tens of millions of people around the world. The company has cited a network upgrade gone awry as the root cause of the incident. Incidents such as the Microsoft 365 outage are a natural consequence of businesses and governments allowing key digital systems to become centralised all over the world. The internet remains, and was pioneered as, a network of networks. If one business’s networks went down, the reasoning went, others would not fall like dominos: everyone was, after all, connected to everyone else. But the economics have long been prohibitive, with dedicated servers and web-connected infrastructure infeasible for all but the largest businesses, with even those firms seeking the enticing cost savings from socialised infrastructure. That made sense: the internet made shared infrastructure more economical, allowing hardware and maintenance costs to be spread so far and wide that at a per-user level prices have been negligible. Competition among major cloud providers, the few that remain at Microsoft’s scale, have kept prices affordable for enterprise software for all shades of organisations.

Digital services have grown more sophisticated, and more deeply integrated into the economy as this centralisation unfolded. But the downside is that, regardless of the sophistication and professionalism of any company, mistakes happen, and the scale of these mistakes can quickly cascade over to the entire economy. There are societal and organisational lessons to be gleaned from these episodes. There is no such thing as a reliable vendor. Governments must also draw a cyber sovereignty lesson here that does not simply entail swapping a global vendor for a domestic one. It is the subversion of the internet’s architecture that is at the root of these incidents. Investing in resilience — and shielding critical operations from destabilising disruptions, no matter how improbable — should inform attitudes to digital systems. As a new generation of AI data centres is poised to supercharge the centralised systems of yesteryear, it is all the more imperative to mitigate even occasional vagaries of large systems.

articles.title: Advocates, traders protest in Vaniyambadi for additional district court
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: At present, Vaniyambadi has three lower courts that are located in different areas in the town
Advocates, traders and residents staged a protest near a bus terminus in Vaniyambadi town on Thursday, demanding an additional district court and a permanent building for the court complex.

The protest was held in the wake of the onset of the Northeast monsoon, when it could be risky to conduct court proceedings at the dilapidated Judicial Magistrate court. “Work to build a permanent court complex should be expedited. An additional district court should also be set up in the court complex”, said A.C. Devakumar, president, Bar Association (Vaniyambadi).

At present, Vaniyambadi has three lower courts that are located in different areas in the town. Each court, on an average, is located at least 1.5 km away from the other court. It has resulted in hardship for litigants, advocates, and court staff to commute from one court to another as some petitioners have cases in different courts that will be taken up on the same day.

The Judicial Magistrate Court, the oldest among three courts, was located in the Government Estate since the 1920s. The District Munsif court, formed in 1995, was functioning from a rented room in the Government Commercial Tax building. The subordinate court that was created in 2009 was also operating from a rented room in the town.

Every day, on an average, more than 150 litigants, mostly from Vaniyambadi taluk that comprises 45 villages, visit these courts. Around 75 advocates are working as regular practitioners. On an average, over 100 cases come up at each court every day. Currently, 1,500 - 2,000 cases are pending before each of these three courts.

Case bundles and court records get damaged during monsoon as the building is inundated. The court also does not have an audio system, to call for cases or parties. As a result, many litigants wait for long hours or leave as they are unsure about whether their case has been called.

articles.title: Kerala High Court disposes of PILs against reconstitution of Waqf Board
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The High Court had refused to stay the reconstitution of the board in October
A Division Bench of the Kerala High Court on Thursday disposed of all public interest litigations (PILs) related to the reconstitution of the Kerala State Waqf Board.

The Bench observed that the reconstitution of the board had given rise to a fresh cause of action, following which the aggrieved parties had filed writ petitions. It said the petitions were required to be heard by a Single Judge in accordance with the roster.

The High Court had in October refused to stay the reconstitution of the board. The court was considering appeals filed by former board chairperson K.S. Hamza and member C.K. Usman Haji against a Single Bench order refusing to stay the reconstitution.
The court had then held that a stay could not be granted as the new board had taken charge. The State had reconstituted the board on October 16 and nominated nine new members.

The High Court had refused to stay the reconstitution of the board in October

A Division Bench of the Kerala High Court on Thursday disposed of all public interest litigations (PILs) related to the reconstitution of the Kerala State Waqf Board.

The Bench observed that the reconstitution of the board had given rise to a fresh cause of action, following which the aggrieved parties had filed writ petitions. It said the petitions were required to be heard by a Single Judge in accordance with the roster.

The High Court had in October refused to stay the reconstitution of the board. The court was considering appeals filed by former board chairperson K.S. Hamza and member C.K. Usman Haji against a Single Bench order refusing to stay the reconstitution.

The court had then held that a stay could not be granted as the new board had taken charge. The State had reconstituted the board on October 16 and nominated nine new members.

articles.title: Set aside differences and oppose Mekedatu dam, says TNCC president
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: He also questions Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s silence when Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar spoke in favour of the project in his presence

Tamil Nadu Congress Committee (TNCC) president B. Manickam Tagore on Thursday said the party would oppose the proposed Mekedatu dam across the Cauvery and called for all political parties in Tamil Nadu to unite against the project instead of indulging in mutual accusations.
He said the project could spell a death knell for the Cauvery delta and turn the region drought-prone. The Congress was clear that it would not compromise on Tamil Nadu’s legitimate rights, he said.

Calling for a united stand, he urged Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay and former Chief Ministers M.K. Stalin, Edappadi K. Palaniswami, and O. Panneerselvam to join hands in opposing the project. He also questioned Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s silence when Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar spoke in favour of the project in his presence.

Referring to the recent meeting between three Tamil Nadu Ministers and Union Minister C.R. Paatil, Mr. Tagore said the State government should share the outcome of the discussions with the Assembly, its alliance partners, and the people.

Mr. Tagore also criticised the AIADMK for not participating in the all-party meeting and meeting of MPs convened by the Tamil Nadu government on delimitation, while subsequently supporting the Assembly resolution on the issue.

On the Congress-TVK relationship, he said the prominence given to Mr. Vijay at Sonia Gandhi’s book launch in Delhi reflected the strong and long-term ties between the two parties. He added that the Congress was committed to helping the government fulfil its promise of building a strong and drug-free Tamil Nadu.

articles.title: Speakers recall Sathya Sai Baba’s emphasis on vital role of women in society
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Noted actor Rashmika Mandanna and former Chief Secretary to Government of Karnataka Vandita Sharma participate in the Ladies’ Day observed as part of the ongoing birth centenary celebrations of Sri Sathya Sai Baba in Puttaparthi
Noted actor Rashmika Mandanna participated in the Ladies’ Day observed as part of the ongoing birth centenary celebrations of Sri Sathya Sai Baba, at Prashanti Nilayam in Puttaparthi on Thursday.

Apart from the cultural presentations, speakers who addressed the gathering in Sai Kulwant Hall highlighted Sri Sathya Sai Baba’s emphasis on the dignity, inner strength and vital role of women in society.

The girl students of the Sri Sathya Sai Institute of Higher Learning, Anantapur campus, presented a band performance. Vandita Sharma, former Chief Secretary to the Government of Karnataka, and Neelam Desai, senior cardiac surgeon at the Sri Sathya Sai Institute of Higher Medical Sciences, Prasanthigram, participated in the traditional lighting of the lamp marking the occasion.

Delivering the welcome address, Dr. Neelam Desai recalled Sri Sathya Sai Baba’s message on the first Ladies’ Day, observed on November 19, 1995. “Among human beings, it is a privilege to be born as a woman,” she said quoting Sri Sathya Sai Baba, and highlighted the qualities of love, sacrifice, courage and perseverance that women embody.

She shared the story of Ramabai Ranveer, a 47-year-old mother from Ambajogai, Maharashtra, who won a local barefoot running event to earn ₹3,000 for books and educational supplies for her daughters. She also recalled Samudra Pradakshina, the pioneering all-women tri-service circumnavigation sailing expedition flagged off on September 11, 2025.
Girl students of Sri Sathya Sai Higher Secondary School and Smt. Eswaramma High School presented cultural offerings as part of the morning programme.

Addressing the gathering, Ms. Vandita Sharma noted that Ladies’ Day celebrates women’s inherent strength and contributions to family and society, while encouraging them to recognise their potential and express it with confidence and commitment.

She appreciated the Sri Sathya Sai Media Centre for making Baba’s discourses readily accessible, enabling devotees to draw guidance from His teachings. She urged everyone to put His message into practice in daily life.

Ms. Rashmika Mandanna shared how her association with the family of actor Vijay Deverakonda had brought her closer to Baba and His teachings. Spending time with the family, she said, had helped her understand their devotion and appreciate the relevance of Baba’s message.
She emphasised the importance of spiritual and emotional strength, along with an unwavering commitment to human values.

articles.title: Anthropic soars in Wall Street debut despite AI jitters
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Anthropic raised a record $81.3 billion in the offering. The IPO price valued the maker of the Claude chatbot at about $1.5 trillion, including employee stock options and restricted shares. At around $98 a share, the company was worth about $1.8 trillion

Anthropic shares opened 34% higher in their Nasdaq debut on Thursday (November 19, 2026), briefly valuing the AI giant around $2 trillion, as investors shrugged off the Nvidia spy scandal and fears of a tech bubble.

The shares opened at $111.50 before settling minutes into trading at around $98, up 18% from the $83 at which the company priced its shares on Wednesday (November 18, 2026), already above its expected range.

Anthropic raised a record $81.3 billion in the offering. The IPO price valued the maker of the Claude chatbot at about $1.5 trillion, including employee stock options and restricted shares. At around $98 a share, the company was worth about $1.8 trillion.

The debut marks a milestone in the AI boom. A company founded five years ago by OpenAI defectors worried about AI safety has become the first of the leading model developers to list on Wall Street, at a valuation rivalling decades-old tech brands.
The listing, under the ticker “ANT,” gives ordinary investors their first chance to bet directly on a stand-alone AI giant.

“Today puts the company in a stronger financial position, and in doing so, only strengthens our resolve to do the right thing,” chief executive Dario Amodei said at the Nasdaq in New York’s Times Square, underlining the company’s priority of promoting safe AI.
The offering surpasses the $75 billion that Elon Musk’s SpaceX raised in its June IPO at a valuation of $1.77 trillion.

SpaceX’s total ultimately rose to $86 billion after its underwriters exercised an option to buy additional shares. Anthropic has granted its underwriters a similar option, which would lift its total to about $93.5 billion.

“This may be the breath of fresh air that the tech trade needed to move beyond the fog of artificial intelligence that we’ve been living in for the last couple of weeks,” Art Hogan of B. Riley Wealth Management told AFP .
The strong demand comes even as AI stocks have swung sharply, with investors questioning whether heavy spending on the technology will pay off.

Anthropic raised a record $81.3 billion in the offering. The IPO price valued the maker of the Claude chatbot at about $1.5 trillion, including employee stock options and restricted shares. At around $98 a share, the company was worth about $1.8 trillion

Anthropic shares opened 34% higher in their Nasdaq debut on Thursday (November 19, 2026), briefly valuing the AI giant around $2 trillion, as investors shrugged off the Nvidia spy scandal and fears of a tech bubble.

The shares opened at $111.50 before settling minutes into trading at around $98, up 18% from the $83 at which the company priced its shares on Wednesday (November 18, 2026), already above its expected range.

Anthropic raised a record $81.3 billion in the offering. The IPO price valued the maker of the Claude chatbot at about $1.5 trillion, including employee stock options and restricted shares. At around $98 a share, the company was worth about $1.8 trillion.

The debut marks a milestone in the AI boom. A company founded five years ago by OpenAI defectors worried about AI safety has become the first of the leading model developers to list on Wall Street, at a valuation rivalling decades-old tech brands.

The listing, under the ticker “ANT,” gives ordinary investors their first chance to bet directly on a stand-alone AI giant.

“Today puts the company in a stronger financial position, and in doing so, only strengthens our resolve to do the right thing,” chief executive Dario Amodei said at the Nasdaq in New York’s Times Square, underlining the company’s priority of promoting safe AI.

The offering surpasses the $75 billion that Elon Musk’s SpaceX raised in its June IPO at a valuation of $1.77 trillion.

SpaceX’s total ultimately rose to $86 billion after its underwriters exercised an option to buy additional shares. Anthropic has granted its underwriters a similar option, which would lift its total to about $93.5 billion.

“This may be the breath of fresh air that the tech trade needed to move beyond the fog of artificial intelligence that we’ve been living in for the last couple of weeks,” Art Hogan of B. Riley Wealth Management told AFP .

The strong demand comes even as AI stocks have swung sharply, with investors questioning whether heavy spending on the technology will pay off.

fullParagraphs: The Claude maker priced its shares at $83 apiece, implying an equity valuation of about $1.03 trillion based on outstanding shares, with trading scheduled to begin on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT on November 19

Anthropic, the maker of artificial intelligence (AI) chatbot Claude, has priced its initial public offering (IPO) at $83 a share, valuing the offering at approximately $81.34 billion, according to an announcement by the company on November 18.

The company said its shares were expected to begin trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market on November 19 under the ticker symbol ANT. The offering is expected to close on November 20, subject to customary closing conditions.

According to Anthropic’s announcement, the offering comprises 980 million shares of Class A common stock. Of these, 956.35 million shares are being sold by the company and 23.65 million by existing shareholders. Anthropic said it would not receive any proceeds from the sale of shares by the selling shareholders.

At the IPO price of $83 a share, the company’s portion of the offering is valued at approximately $79.38 billion, while the shares sold by existing shareholders are valued at approximately $1.96 billion. These figures are before underwriting discounts and expenses.
At $83 a share, Anthropic’s overall equity value works out to approximately $1.03 trillion, based on the total number of shares outstanding after the IPO.
Anthropic has also given the banks (underwriters) managing the IPO the option to purchase an additional 147 million shares within 30 days, potentially increasing the size of the offering.
Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley are the lead underwriters for the IPO, with JPMorgan, Citigroup, Barclays and other investment banks also participating, according to the SEC filing.
The IPO comes amid growing investor concerns over the sustainability of the AI investment boom and whether technology companies can generate sufficient returns from their infrastructure spending.
On November 5, the Nasdaq Composite fell 5.5%, wiping out trillions of dollars in market value, while NVIDIA shares declined 9% and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index dropped 12%.

Earlier, on October 29, Alphabet shares plunged 12.6%, wiping out approximately $500 billion in market value after its quarterly results raised concerns over its advertising business and the cash-flow impact of rising AI investments. The sell-off reflected broader concerns over the valuations of AI-linked companies and the returns from their heavy spending on data centres and computing infrastructure.

articles.title: Cyclone ‘Akvan’ updates: Three lakh evacuated, 423 rescue teams deployed as cyclone heads to Odisha
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The severe cyclonic storm is likely to cross north Andhra Pradesh and south Odisha coasts close to Gopalpur by noon on November 20

The Disaster Management Unit of Union Ministry of Communications has instructed telecom service providers to activate Intra Circle Roaming facility in Ganjam, Gajapati, Puri, Kendrapara, Jagatsinghpur and Khordha district on November 20.

As per information provided by Odisha Space Applications Centre, as many as 941 places have been identified as landslip prone areas including 211 in Gajapati district, Ganjam (169), Rayagada (169), Kandhamal (163) Koraput (151) and Malkangiri (78), said Mr. Pujari while reviewing preparation for cyclone “Akvan” on November 19, 2026.

Ghat roads (hill passes) such as Kalinga and Gajalbadi connecting Ganjam and Kandhamal districts have been barricaded, apprehending landslides. Red warning for heavy to very heavy rainfall has been issued for districts such as Kendrapada, Jagatsinghpur, Puri, Ganjam, Gajapati, and Kandhamal.

“Water Resources Department has started depleting reservoirs in districts to be affected by the cyclone. Engineers are continuously monitoring situation while technical teams have been deployed. Two gates of major dam and 23 gates of different medium irrigation dams are kept opened,” said Odisha Chief Secretary Anu Garg. - Satyasundar Barik

Severe Cyclonic Storm ‘Akvan’ over the westcentral Bay of Bengal moved northwards at a speed of 13 kmph during the past six hours and was centred over the same region at 5.30 p.m. on November 19, 2026, according to the India Meteorological Department (IMD).
The cyclone is likely to move north-northwestwards and cross North Andhra Pradesh and South Odisha coasts close to Gopalpur by noon on November 20.

Revenue and Disaster Management Minister Suresh Pujari informed that senior bureaucrats were assigned different districts to monitor rescue-and-restoration activities, besides monitoring situations from State Emergency Operation Centres. In Ganjam and Gajapati districts, 17 satellite phones were provided to key persons to remain in contact if communication network is snapped due to cyclone.

As part of the preparedness measures, 70 Cell-on-Wheels (CoW) units, 197 Mobile Diesel Generator (DG) sets and 61 support teams have been deployed to strengthen telecom infrastructure and ensure continuity of communication during the cyclone. The Disaster Management Unit of Union Ministry of Communications has instructed telecom service providers to activate Intra Circle Roaming facility in Ganjam, Gajapati, Puri, Kendrapara, Jagatsinghpur and Khordha district on November 20. - Satyasundar Barik

Odisha on Thursday (November 19, 2026) geared up to tackle Severe Cyclonic Storm ‘Akvan’, which is expected to cross the State’s coast near Gopalpur by noon on November 20, with heavy rain and maximum sustained wind speeds of 90-100 kmph, gusting to 110 kmph. The State shifted close to three lakh people to safer places by evening.

As many as 60 units Odisha Disaster Rapid Action Force, 14 units of National Disaster Response Force and 221 teams of State fire services have been positioned at vulnerable areas to carry out rescue and restoration operation soon after ‘Akvan’ passed through the State.

articles.title: Trinamool party symbol row: Abhishek Banerjee says twin flower symbol will return in seven days
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Leader of the Opposition in the West Bengal Assembly Ritabrata Banerjee said that the symbol does not belong to either faction and Mr. Banerjee will not be able to stake claim over the symbol in seven births

The two rival factions of the Trinamool Congress have become embroiled in a war of words over the party’s twin-flower symbol that has been frozen by the Election Commission of India (ECI). Diamond Harbour MP Abhishek Banerjee and Mamata All India Trinamool Congress on November 18 said that the original electoral symbol of the party will ultimately remain with Mamata Banerjee.

“The original name and electoral symbol had always been with Mamata Banerjee and will continue to remain so in the future. Just wait for seven days. We will prove how manipulations were made in filing affidavits to establish the right over the original party name and original electoral symbol. We will display that on the big screen,” Mr. Banerjee told media persons.

Mr. Banerjee has claimed that the faction of the party led by Ritabrata Banerjee filed affidavits with the help of the West Bengal Police. The Diamond Harbour MP had claimed that the alleged attack on his residence on November 7 was intended to interfere with the filing of affidavits, staking a claim over the affidavits.

Leader of the Opposition in the West Bengal Assembly Ritabrata Banerjee said that the symbol does not belong to either faction and Mr. Banerjee will not be able to stake claim over the symbol in seven births.
“He has said that they will get the symbol in seven days, they will not get the symbol in seven births,” the LOP, which represents the Democratic Trinamool Congress, said.

The ECI on September 17, 2026, had barred both factions, the Mamata Banerjee-led faction and the Ritabrata Banerjee-led faction of the party, from using the party symbol and name in the bypolls in Nandigram and Rejinagar in West Bengal which were scheduled on October 6. The very next day, on September 18, the Mamata faction got the name ‘Mamata All India Trinamool Congress’ with ‘football player’ as its symbol , while the Ritabrata grouping was allotted the name ‘Democratic Trinamool Congress’ with the symbol ‘envelope’.

Both the factions of the Trinamool Congress have submitted truckloads of affidavits to the ECI, which includes support by party members, MPs and MLAs. Ritabrata Banerjee claims support of 65 of the 80 MLAs of the party. The faction of Mamata Banerjee has the support of a handful of MLAs and MPs who have not defected to NCPI or joined the BJP after the West Bengal Assembly polls of 2026.

articles.title: Time to protect eroding coastlines
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Nearly 31% (318.96 km) of Andhra Pradesh’s coastline is eroding, with about 91.6 km falling into the ‘high erosion’ category. While the losses are concentrated in the delta districts of Kakinada, West Godavari, and Krishna, the coastal port district of Visakhapatnam is also facing the issue. Paul Nicodemus explores how decades of port development, changing wave patterns, and cyclones have contributed to the erosion of the City of Destiny’s beaches

For Professor B.S.R. Reddy, who retired from the Department of Meteorology and Oceanography at Andhra University, reaching the sea from the Beach Road in the early 1960s meant walking at least half a kilometre over high dunes—an exciting journey up one sandhill and down another. Residing at the Pithapuram Beach Hostels as a student, opposite the site where the INS Kursura Submarine Museum now stands, he recalls hearing the crashing waves from the road amidst the shouts of fellow students playing football on the sand, even though the sea itself was hidden from view. Today, he says, there are “no beaches” along stretches of that road, and the waves strike it directly.

Beyond the disappearing stretches of sand, the consequences of coastal erosion are being felt not only by those who depend on the sea for their livelihoods, but also by the State, which is steadily losing land to the encroaching sea.

For instance, earlier this month the seaward edge of the beach road near the museum had been cut away, with rubble and boulders strewn across the sand below. Near RK Beach, waves had eroded a sand bank beneath a row of coconut palms, exposing the bases of trees and cable conduits.

This loss is also documented in the Shoreline Change Atlas of Andhra Pradesh, published in February 2024 by the National Centre for Coastal Research (NCCR), under the Union Ministry of Earth Sciences. Using satellite imagery, the agency mapped 1,027.58 km of Andhra Pradesh’s coastline between 1990 and 2022. It found that 31 per cent (318.96 km) is eroding, 24.9 per cent is stable, and 44 per cent is gaining sand—with about 91.6 km falling in the “high erosion” category, losing more than five metres a year.

According to the atlas, the losses are concentrated in the delta districts. In Kakinada, 52.8 per cent of the coast is eroding, followed by West Godavari at 52.5 per cent, and Krishna at 43.8 per cent. It mentions that coastal port district Visakhapatnam lies somewhere in between. Of its 70.61 km of coast, 25.9 per cent is eroding, mostly at a rate of 0.5m to 3m a year; 51.3 per cent is stable and 22.8 per cent is gaining sand. The district map identifies one erosion hotspot at Pedanagamayyapalem near Bheemunipatnam.

articles.title: Vizag Junior Literary Fest: Where young minds find their voice
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The seventh edition of Vizag Junior Literary Fest, to be held on November 21 and 22, brings together 20 authors, illustrators and performers as children look forward to creative discoveries and author interactions

What happens when a weekend is spent reading stories, meeting one’s favourite authors and discovering new worlds through books, art and imagination? Hundreds of children in Visakhapatnam are set to find the answer at the Vizag Junior Literary Fest (VJLF). The excitement is as much about stories waiting to be discovered as it is about the friendships, conversations and creative experiences that come with them.

Returning for its seventh edition on November 21 and 22, the festival, organised by Lit Lantern Culture and Literature Society, promises a packed programme featuring 20 speakers and close to 100 sessions. With a fresh line-up of authors, illustrators, performers and artists, the two-day event hopes to turn literature into an immersive experience for children across age groups.
Founder and directors of Vizag Junior Literary Fest Sonal Sarda, Priya Uppalapati and Sandhya Venugopal Godey. | Photo Credit: SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT

For festival directors Sonal Sarda, Priya Uppalapati and Sandhya Venugopal Godey, the larger idea is to create a space where children can connect with literature and, more importantly, with one another.

“The idea is to expose children to a wide spectrum of literature while encouraging genuine human connections in an increasingly device-driven world. We are placing a strong emphasis on free outdoor sessions, where leading speakers will host storytelling sessions, talks and puppet shows, culminating in performances. We want VJLF to remain a space where families and friends can come together, engage and enjoy a nurturing cultural experience,” says Sonal.

This year’s theme centres on hope and collaboration, an idea that runs through both the programming and the festival’s physical setting. At a time when conversations are increasingly divided, the organisers hope to encourage children to listen, share perspectives and discover the value of working together.

“We are witnessing a highly polarised world, which makes conversations more important than ever. From the festival’s set-up to its sessions, we want to create opportunities for dialogue, collaboration and exchange,” she adds.
Parents and children at the author signing section at the previous edition of Vizag Junior Literary Fest in Visakhapatnam. | Photo Credit: SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT

The programming has been tailored to suit different age groups. For children aged four to seven, wonder, hope and excitement take centre stage through musical storytelling, illustration and sessions such as Funny Tales. The eight to 12 age group has the widest range of offerings, from writing and poetry to detective stories, food and friendship. Workshops in mime, clowning, theatre, art, illustration and emotional well-being add to the mix.

For teenagers, the festival moves towards conversations about identity, personal boundaries and the divisions that shape everyday life. Author and filmmaker Samina Mishra’s Lines explores the ideas of belonging, separation and connection, encouraging young readers to look beyond the lines that divide people. Ayisha Begum’s Importance of Boundaries , meanwhile, helps teenagers recognise when to say no and stand by their choices.

articles.title: Tukaram Mundhe withdraws petition after dragging Centre to the court
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: FDA Commissioner Tukaram Mundhe had challenged FSSAI over the constitutional validity of a few regulations. The petition had challenged the creation of a few posts by the Centre, claiming it was against the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006

Two months after deciding to drag the Centre to court over a jurisdiction dispute, the Maharashtra government has taken a call to withdraw its petition, which had accused the Central government of usurping its power and creating new rules in a ‘clandestine manner’.

On September 3, 2026, Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration had filed a petition against FSSAI, challenging the constitutional validity of a few regulations. It had claimed that these regulations had led to the creation of ‘a parallel structure’ which ‘encroached upon the powers and duties of the State Commissioner of Food Safety and his officers.’ On October 29, the government directed officials to withdraw this petition, which had caused a stir as it led to a tussle between the Centre and the State, both governed by the Bharatiya Janata Party.

Political & National Report: Tukaram Mundhe withdraws petition after dragging Centre to the court. This development is a key milestone in India's ongoing legislative, judicial, and constitutional governance framework.

Sixteen weather stations in Srikakulam district recorded more than 100 mm rainfall from Thursday night till 7 a.m. on Friday (November 20, 2026) as the Cyclonic Storm Akvan moved closer to the North Andhra-South Odisha coast.

Odisha Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi chaired an emergency review meeting at the Special Relief Commissioner (SRC) office in Bhubaneswar to assess the state’s preparedness for Cyclone Akvan, as over 3 lakh people have been evacuated from vulnerable areas to safer locations.

fullParagraphs: The major rainfall activity has been concentrated in the district of Srikakulam alone, while a few stations in Vizianagaram, Anakapalli, Kakinada, Visakhapatnam, have recorded light showers

Sixteen weather stations in Srikakulam district recorded more than 100 mm rainfall from Thursday (November 19, 2026) night till 7 a.m. on Friday (November 20, 2026) as the Cyclonic Storm Akvan moved closer to the North Andhra-South Odisha coast.

The major rainfall activity has been concentrated in the district of Srikakulam alone, while a few stations in Vizianagaram, Anakapalli, Kakinada, Visakhapatnam, have recorded light showers. Gales gusting to 100 kmph are prevailing around the cyclone centre, while along the A.P. coast near North Coastal A.P., gales of 90 kmph are prevailng.

According to the India Meteorological Department’s hourly bulletin of 7.30 a.m., Akvan, which weakened into a Cyclonic Storm on Thursday night, began interacting with land an hour ago as the outer bands entered the land. The landfall process(eye of the storm entering the land) may begin by 8.30 a.m.

At present, the system is located over the Bay of Bengal at about 80 km east of Kalingapatnam of A.P., and 130 km south of Gopalpur of Odisha. The system may move further northwards and complete the landfall process near Gopalpur of Odisha by noon.

articles.title: BMC starts demolition of building linked to Dawood Ibrahim in Mumbai
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The building was classified as C-1, a category indicating that the structure was dangerous and required demolition

Haji Ismail Haji Habib Musafirkhana, a building located at Pakmodia street in Mumbai’s Bhendi Bazaar and associated with gangster Dawood Ibrahim was surrounded by heavy police force and yellow barricades as Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) began its demolition on Thursday (November 19, 2026).

The BMC partly demolished the building using human resource, then let the bulldozer to the job. BMC decided to raze the building as it has declared the place dangerously dilapidated (C1 category). The property is associated to gangster Dawood, and is considered to be his old residence before he left India in 1986.
“From 7 am the demolition drive action has started. The area is secured and all safety measures has been taken,” said DCP Manish Kalwaniya

The notice was posted outside the property on Tuesday (November 17, 2026), stating, “The demolition action has been planned on November 18 and 19 under police protection bandobast.” The demolition will take place under Section 354 of the Mumbai Municipal Corporation Act and as per the Bombay High Court’s order from August 31, 2020 to act on the demolition.

Saifee Burhani Upliftment Trust (SBUT) requested BMC to evict its occupants and demolish the structure in accordance with a Bombay High Court order of Aug 2020, stating that building falls under Sector 8 of its cluster redevelopment scheme (redevelopment of Bhendi bazar) and is in dilapidated and dangerous condition, as per the notice of BMC.
The building was used as Musafirkhana in the 1930s, especially for the Haj Yatris.

The conflict lies in the prayer hall, as the residents in the area said the place has been serving as a mosque. The building earlier housed 32 shops on the ground floor and 19 residential flats on the upper storeys. However, now the building remains in a dilapidated condition, while only the ground-floor prayer halls and around 10 rooms on the first floor have been in bad condition.

The SBUT, established in 2009 made an offer of ₹1.10 crore on December 8, 2009 and Haji Ismail Haji Habib Musafirkhana Trust and its trustee Noorani Brother accepted offer on December 24, 2011 by Noorani brothers. In 2015, the Charity Commissioner sanctioned the sale to SBUT for ₹1.10 crore. In 2018, Advocate Sana Baugwala sent SBUT a legal notice on behalf of the shop tenants’ forum with a petition filed in the Bombay HC by “Shop Tenant Forum represented by Fazal Mehmood, comprising about 26 tenants. The court noted the property is unregistered.

The Bombay High Court Division Bench of Justices S.C. Dharmadhikari and R.I. Chagla dismissed the petition on December 11, 2019, which brought to challenge the Charity Commissioner’s November 26, 2015 sanction for the ₹1.10 crore sale of the building to SBUT. It said property stays with SBUT until the Waqf Act status is decided, so it could seek the Charity Commissioner’s sanction. It also noted that Waqf Tribunal was the proper forum for the Waqf question.

“After hearing both sides on this point, we are of the opinion that the petitioners before us are a proposed Forum of Shop Tenants on the ground floor of the building. Considering the fact that the building is dilapidated and that the petitioners are not going to be deprived of the benefits of the redevelopment scheme and rather, they are beneficiaries thereof, after proving their eligibility, they would be provided with permanent alternate accommodation on ownership basis, we are not inclined to continue this interim order. The request in that behalf is rejected,” the Court said in it December 11, 2019 order.

articles.title: U.S. religious freedom panel says ‘India targeting minorities in voter roll revisions’
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: USCIRF is a bipartisan body of ⁠the U.S. government that monitors religious freedom around the world and makes policy recommendations, which are not binding

India has escalated its targeting of religious minorities ‌during a voter list revision that struck off tens of millions ​of names nationwide, a U.S. panel on religious freedom said on ⁠Thursday (November 19, 2026).

“The Indian gov’t is targeting Muslim citizens by removing them from voter rolls, calling them ‘foreigners,’ and now illegally deporting them,” Asif Mahmood, the chair of the U.S. Commission on International Religious Freedom, ‌said in a statement.
India’s voter list revision removed 130 million names, roughly the population of Mexico, in the largest deletion of voters in the ‌country’s history.

Data shows the omissions disproportionately affect Muslims , India’s largest minority, who ‌have ⁠faced what rights groups describe as exclusionary policies and rising discrimination since Prime ⁠Minister Narendra Modi took power in 2014.
The Election Commission of India says it was removing duplicate, deceased, shifted and otherwise ineligible voters and that anyone excluded in error can pursue ​appeals.
The revision has become entangled with ‌a separate drive to identify and expel suspected illegal immigrants, even though removal from the rolls does not itself establish that someone is a foreigner.

“The Indian government’s expulsion of its own citizens based on their Muslim faith is a shocking ‌escalation of tactics that target religious minorities,” said Gene Mills, a commissioner ​on the U.S. panel.
Mr. Mills urged the State Department to designate India as a “country of particular concern.”

USCIRF is a bipartisan body of ⁠the U.S. government that monitors religious freedom around the world and makes policy recommendations, which are not binding. Washington has not acted on its recent recommendations on India.

The Ministry of External Affairs has cast USCIRF as biased. New Delhi has repeatedly dismissed such criticism and called it interference in the country’s internal affairs. The Indian Embassy in Washington did not respond to a request for comment.

articles.title: COP 31: Nations still seeking deeper fossil fuel cuts as climate summit enters final day
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The two-week annual summit, which has so far largely failed to advance any big ideas to move away from fossil fuels — mainly coal, oil and gas — which are contributing to more intense and deadly heat waves, droughts, floods and other disasters, ends on Nov. 20

Negotiators entering the final day of this year's United Nations climate talks in Turkiye are seeking meaningful commitments to address global warming amid warnings that only drastic cuts in fossil fuel emissions can avert its most catastrophic effects.

Friday (November 20, 2026) marks the official end of the two-week annual summit, which has so far largely failed to advance any big ideas to move away from fossil fuels — mainly coal, oil and gas — which are contributing to more intense and deadly heat waves, droughts, floods and other disasters.

A goal introduced this year to increase the share of electricity in total global energy consumption from roughly 21% to 35% by 2035, preferably from renewable energy, also would allow the use of coal and other fossil fuels.

And leaders from countries ravaged by climate change — mostly poorer, vulnerable countries that contributed little to the problem — say a UN fund to help them recover from climate disasters and adapt to a warmer world is not nearly large enough.

articles.title: White House fires cybersecurity chief after widespread outages
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Sean Cairncross’ role will be filled in an acting capacity by current Defense Department Chief Information Officer Kirsten Davies

Cyber security chief Sean Cairncross was fired from his post, a source close to the White House told AFP on Thursday (November 19, 2026), following major outages and growing concerns about AI threats.
U.S. President Donald Trump fully supported the firing because Mr. Cairncross lacked proper credentials to perform the job, the source said.

His role will be filled in an acting capacity by current Defense Department Chief Information Officer Kirsten Davies, who has more appropriate credentials and has been Senate-confirmed, the source said.

In recent days and weeks, major outages in America have disrupted travel, communications and e-commerce for countless users, but also affected a top-secret internal communications network at the National Security Administration.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio congratulated Davies on X, writing: “Congratulations to the new National Cyber Director Kirsten Davies — look forward to working together to strengthen America’s cybersecurity.”
Prior to serving as National Cyber Director, Mr. Cairncross filled various roles as a White House insider during Trump’s first term.
Prior to that, MR. Cairncross worked as the Republican National Committee’s Chief Operating Officer for the 2016 election cycle.

articles.title: California Attorney General subpoenas Nvidia over chips, former CEO’s affair
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The California Department of Justice said it is asking Nvidia whether its advanced chips or confidential information may have gone to China and whether Nvidia misled investors and the public
California Attorney General Rob Bonta has issued an investigative subpoena to Nvidia related to former CEO Jensen Huang's affair with a suspected Chinese spy .

The California Department of Justice said on Thursday (November 19, 2026) it is asking Nvidia whether its advanced chips or confidential information may have gone to China and whether Nvidia misled investors and the public.
Ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang acknowledges ‘mistakes,’ signals interest in return if company chooses
Trump says ‘would not mind’ Huang being reinstated at Nvidia
How Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's extramarital affair could cause collateral damage in Washington

"The conduct of Nvidia and its former CEO raises bright red flags, including about the ways in which the company may have misled investors. My office is investigating whether Nvidia or Jensen Huang's actions resulted in China obtaining advanced chips or confidential information — and if Nvidia misled investors and the public about this risk, in violation of the law," Bonta said in a statement.
"Nvidia is in a messy, transnational situation but the underlying principle of our corporate securities law is clear: Companies cannot mislead their investors."

On Tuesday (November 17, 2026), key House lawmakers said that Huang has voluntarily agreed to appear for transcribed interviews as the company faces intensifying national scrutiny over sales of its advanced computer chips.
Mr. Huang will appear before congressional committees on December 1, followed by the company's general counsel, Tim Teter, on December 2.
Nvidia did not immediately respond to a message for comment on Thursday (November 19, 2026).

Anthropic’s debut, the largest IPO on record, was priced ‌on late Wednesday (November 18, 2026) at $83 per share and was widely viewed as the next high bar to clear for the AI trade.
