articles.title: Going public on AI: On Anthropic IPO
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: India can no longer afford its silence on the multi-trillion dollar AI arms race

The Initial Public Offering (IPO) of Anthropic , PBC is a mile marker in the arms race to develop superintelligent systems driven by generative AI . Traders valued the firm at $1.27 trillion, a denomination that is bound to become more and more familiar in an industry backed by an endless appetite for capital and unprecedented forms of financialisation. Anthropic’s statements emphasise warnings on the safety of its systems and the consequences of unbridled development of advanced systems. In the history of the development of this technology, this PR spin may just be a blip. After all, their testing has led to AI agents that have broken out of sandboxes and infected unsuspecting organisations’ internal systems: a deluge of agentic chaos that is already a reality has led to little signs of the firm backing its words with action. A familiar trend is playing out, with open source LLMs showing frontier capabilities that can back their erratic impulses, appearing in the space of just months, or sometimes weeks. Advocates of pacing the frontier and managing these emerging risks have been marginalised in a way that has little precedent in this century. It is time for governments to get involved, and specifically, for India to raise its voice on these risks, loudly and unequivocally.

While India’s AI industry is nascent, its positions on international forums carry the weight of a sixth of humanity. A mix of cynical calculations and practical considerations have blunted the use of that voice, for example in the U.S.’s hugely destabilising war of choice against Iran, and Israel’s ongoing genocide in Gaza. In taking a strong position on what could be the defining transformation of this decade, India has little to lose, and a lot to contribute. India’s AI policies are geared towards diffusion and research of helpful capabilities that can trickle down to the common citizen. The capabilities that the Union government and State governments seek to boost by leveraging AI are removed from the frontier research wreaking havoc within the information security profession around the world. Out-of-control AI agents promise, moreover, significant disruption to outdated government and private systems online. While India has little commercial leverage to curb San Francisco’s accelerationism, its voice is sure to be noticed. India’s focus on AI in international fora, such as the AI Impact Summit in Delhi, has been on consensus. This approach must change. India cannot be silent amid a U.S.-China technological race which could lead to catastrophic damage. New Delhi must not allow the U.S. to stop it from pushing for AI safety.

articles.summary: India can no longer afford its silence on the multi-trillion dollar AI arms race
articles.keyPoints:
• India can no longer afford its silence on the multi-trillion dollar AI arms race
• The Initial Public Offering (IPO) of Anthropic , PBC is a mile marker in the arms race to develop superintelligent systems driven by generative AI . Traders valued the firm at $1.27 trillion, a denomination that is bound to become more and more familiar in an industry backed by an endless appetite for capital and unprecedented forms of financialisation. Anthropic’s statements emphasise warnings on the safety of its systems and the consequences of unbridled development of advanced systems. In the history of the development of this technology, this PR spin may just be a blip. After all, their testing has led to AI agents that have broken out of sandboxes and infected unsuspecting organisations’ internal systems: a deluge of agentic chaos that is already a reality has led to little signs of the firm backing its words with action. A familiar trend is playing out, with open source LLMs showing frontier capabilities that can back their erratic impulses, appearing in the space of just months, or sometimes weeks. Advocates of pacing the frontier and managing these emerging risks have been marginalised in a way that has little precedent in this century. It is time for governments to get involved, and specifically, for India to raise its voice on these risks, loudly and unequivocally.
• While India’s AI industry is nascent, its positions on international forums carry the weight of a sixth of humanity. A mix of cynical calculations and practical considerations have blunted the use of that voice, for example in the U.S.’s hugely destabilising war of choice against Iran, and Israel’s ongoing genocide in Gaza. In taking a strong position on what could be the defining transformation of this decade, India has little to lose, and a lot to contribute. India’s AI policies are geared towards diffusion and research of helpful capabilities that can trickle down to the common citizen. The capabilities that the Union government and State governments seek to boost by leveraging AI are removed from the frontier research wreaking havoc within the information security profession around the world. Out-of-control AI agents promise, moreover, significant disruption to outdated government and private systems online. While India has little commercial leverage to curb San Francisco’s accelerationism, its voice is sure to be noticed. India’s focus on AI in international fora, such as the AI Impact Summit in Delhi, has been on consensus. This approach must change. India cannot be silent amid a U.S.-China technological race which could lead to catastrophic damage. New Delhi must not allow the U.S. to stop it from pushing for AI safety.

The 16th round of commercial coal mine auctions has attracted 83 bids for 17 coal blocks with 20 first-time bidders seeking to enter commercial coal mining, signalling fresh interest in the sector.
The Union Coal Ministry said on Friday that 17 blocks offered in the latest round received 83 bids. In addition, the second attempt to auction one coal block from the 15th round attracted two bids.
Taking the 26 blocks covered by the auction process into account, the number of bids has quadrupled compared with the previous round, the ministry said.
The 16th round of commercial coal mine auctions was launched on September 17, offering 25 blocks, comprising 21 fully explored and four partially explored mines.

“Competition in the current round has been intense, with 16 of the 26 blocks attracting multiple bids. The round has also brought 20 first-time bidders into the commercial coal mining regime, a clear sign that the sector continues to draw new capital and new players,” the ministry said in a statement.

Since the introduction of the commercial coal mining auction regime in June 2020, the government has auctioned 145 coal mines across 15 rounds. These mines are estimated to generate annual revenues of around ₹47,500 crore, according to government estimates.

articles.title: CEA flags need to align capital markets with India’s development priorities
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: Equity market capitalisation stood at around 130% of GDP, while the corporate bond market accounted for only about 16%.

Chief Economic Adviser V. Anantha Nageswaran has called for a greater role for Indian capital markets in channelising household savings into productive investments, stressing the importance of patient capital in meeting the country’s long-term development needs.

Speaking at the CII Financial Summit in Mumbai, Mr. Nageswaran said sectors such as infrastructure, manufacturing, agriculture and mineral exploration required long-term financing, given their extended investment horizons.
Highlighting the imbalance in India’s financial markets, he pointed out that equity market capitalisation stood at around 130% of GDP, while the corporate bond market accounted for only about 16%.

While acknowledging that technology had improved market access, settlement systems and transaction security, he said these advances had not necessarily translated into better outcomes for investors or the real economy.

“A safer machine is not the same as a better outcome,” he said, emphasising that technological innovation should ultimately strengthen the capital market’s core function of converting savings into productive investments.
Cautioning against a consumption-led economic model, Mr. Nageswaran said, “An economy that is consumption-oriented may not be the most suited one for India’s development context.”

Echoing the need to promote long-term savings, Gaurav Mathur, founder and managing director of SafeGold, called for tax incentives to encourage investors to hold financial assets for longer periods. He stressed that savings policies should reflect individuals’ financial circumstances and different stages of life.

“It’s a matter of constructive partnership between regulators and financial intermediaries, where you incentivise long-term saving behaviour at the appropriate stages in life,” Mr. Mathur said, adding that incentives should particularly target wealthier individuals with greater capacity to save.

Meanwhile, Nilesh Shah, managing director of Kotak Mahindra Asset Management Company and part-time member of the Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister, underscored the need to strengthen financial literacy and encourage voluntary pension savings. He said these measures were increasingly important amid uncertainties over employment and income in a technology-driven economy.

articles.title: How AI could reshape global growth and productivity
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: A key expected impact of AI is an unprecedented rise in labour productivity, as its success as a technological revolution is premised on such an increase; what remains to be seen is how pervasive its impact will be across different sectors of the economy

Many have likened the artificial intelligence (AI) phenomenon to the inventions of the steam engine or internal combustion engine in the 18th and 19th centuries, respectively. Only time can tell whether AI is epochal of that kind. In this two-part piece, we discuss the possible impact it may have on the global economy as a whole.

A key impact of AI is considered to be an unprecedented rise in labour productivity. In fact, if there is one purpose AI is supposed to serve, it is enhancing labour productivity multifold. Since labour productivity is a key variable in this puzzle, consider what it constitutes of (Box 1) . It is a ratio of output and workers employed. Now this ratio can rise in three different ways — a rise in output for a given number of workers employed (rise in the numerator); a loss of jobs which leads to a fall in the denominator; more jobs are created, but the output rises faster than the jobs (while both the numerator and the denominator are rising, the numerator rises faster than the denominator).

There is usually a distinction drawn between a case where there is a net loss of jobs versus one where jobs grow, but the output grows even faster. The latter is preferred over the former. Even though AI may displace white-collar workers, it may generate more jobs for the blue-collar workers, so in the net there may not be a job loss with AI adoption across the economy. However, for the argument we make below, it does not matter which of the three sources leads to a rise in productivity. Why should the rise in labour productivity matter? There are two contrasting takes on this question in the economics discipline.

One which argues that productivity growth increases the growth of output in the economy. The idea is simple. Growth of output is a function of its two inputs — labour and capital. Since capital enhances the productivity of labour, the rate at which output can grow is the sum of the growth of the labour force and its productivity. So, if the workforce grows at 2% and productivity at 4%, the economy would stabilise at 6% growth over time. And if the rate of labour productivity rises, according to this framework, growth in the economy rises pari passu (Graph 1a).

Between the three variables — output growth, labour growth and productivity growth — output growth adjusts to the other two. This is what Robert Solow, a celebrated economist and a Nobel laureate, showed in a seminal paper on growth theory. What he did not explain though was why and where did this labour productivity rise come from. Much later, his successors argued that the growth of labour productivity depends on investment in human capital, research and development, patent regimes, etc., what came to be known as endogenous growth theories.

📈 Economic, Banking & Finance 📅 20 Nov 2026 ⏱️ 4 Min Read

📰 How AI could reshape global growth and productivity

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
🔮 Futuristic Word Radar: Paragraph ke kisi bhi English word par Double-Click karein — turant uska Hinglish Meaning + Picture screen par dekhein!

A key expected impact of AI is an unprecedented rise in labour productivity, as its success as a technological revolution is premised on such an increase; what remains to be seen is how pervasive its impact will be across different sectors of the economy

Many have likened the artificial intelligence (AI) phenomenon to the inventions of the steam engine or internal combustion engine in the 18th and 19th centuries, respectively. Only time can tell whether AI is epochal of that kind. In this two-part piece, we discuss the possible impact it may have on the global economy as a whole.

A key impact of AI is considered to be an unprecedented rise in labour productivity. In fact, if there is one purpose AI is supposed to serve, it is enhancing labour productivity multifold. Since labour productivity is a key variable in this puzzle, consider what it constitutes of (Box 1) . It is a ratio of output and workers employed. Now this ratio can rise in three different ways — a rise in output for a given number of workers employed (rise in the numerator); a loss of jobs which leads to a fall in the denominator; more jobs are created, but the output rises faster than the jobs (while both the numerator and the denominator are rising, the numerator rises faster than the denominator).

There is usually a distinction drawn between a case where there is a net loss of jobs versus one where jobs grow, but the output grows even faster. The latter is preferred over the former. Even though AI may displace white-collar workers, it may generate more jobs for the blue-collar workers, so in the net there may not be a job loss with AI adoption across the economy. However, for the argument we make below, it does not matter which of the three sources leads to a rise in productivity. Why should the rise in labour productivity matter? There are two contrasting takes on this question in the economics discipline.

One which argues that productivity growth increases the growth of output in the economy. The idea is simple. Growth of output is a function of its two inputs — labour and capital. Since capital enhances the productivity of labour, the rate at which output can grow is the sum of the growth of the labour force and its productivity. So, if the workforce grows at 2% and productivity at 4%, the economy would stabilise at 6% growth over time. And if the rate of labour productivity rises, according to this framework, growth in the economy rises pari passu (Graph 1a).

Between the three variables — output growth, labour growth and productivity growth — output growth adjusts to the other two. This is what Robert Solow, a celebrated economist and a Nobel laureate, showed in a seminal paper on growth theory. What he did not explain though was why and where did this labour productivity rise come from. Much later, his successors argued that the growth of labour productivity depends on investment in human capital, research and development, patent regimes, etc., what came to be known as endogenous growth theories.

articles.title: Estonia to close border with Russia, Moscow decries 'new Iron Curtain'
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: NATO and EU member ‌Estonia on November 15 accused Russian security services of staging an attempted ‌arson ⁠attack on an Estonian defence company, in what it said ⁠was the second such incident this year

Estonia will close its road border crossings with Russia on security grounds for at least six months, the Baltic country's government ‌said on Friday (November 20, 2026), prompting a warning from Moscow that it would respond with political and diplomatic measures.

NATO and EU member ‌Estonia on Sunday (November 15, 2026) accused Russian security services of staging an attempted ‌arson ⁠attack on an Estonian defence company, in what it said ⁠was the second such incident this year.
This would help address the wider security situation and limit Russia's ability to ​organise further attacks, Estonian Interior Minister ‌Igor Taro told a press conference.
"Russian security services are intimidating and trying to recruit our citizens who are travelling through our border checkpoints. This is something we cannot tolerate anymore," Mr. Taro said.
The Kremlin has ‌denied any involvement in the weekend arson attack.
Foreign Ministry spokeswoman ​Maria Zakharova on Friday (November 20, 2026) said that Russia would respond with political and diplomatic measures if Estonia went ahead with the ⁠closure.
"Such moves are tantamount to attempts to erect a new Iron Curtain under the false pretence of some sort of threat from the East," ‌Ms. Zakharova said.
Estonia, a strong supporter of Ukraine, currently has five crossing points where travellers can enter or leave Russia, according to the government.
Estonia's northern neighbour Finland shut its Russia border crossings in 2023, and has kept them closed since then, while southern Baltic nations Latvia and Lithuania maintain open crossings.

Thousands of people living in Estonia have family in ‌Russia or vice versa, as legacies of the Soviet era. The crossing at Narva, a ​majority Russian-speaking city on the Estonian side of the border, is also used by people travelling from further afield in ⁠Europe to reach St. Petersburg a few hours' drive away.

articles.title: Pakistan Army chief Munir vows to eliminate terrorism from country
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Pakistan overall witnessed a significant decline in terrorism-related violence during October, with attacks falling by 37%, deaths resulting from these attacks declining by 57%, and injuries decreasing by 71% compared to September, said Dawn newspaper report

Pakistan’s Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir on Friday (November 20, 2026) expressed the “unwavering resolve” of the security forces to eliminate terrorism from the country during a visit to the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province.
Mr. Munir, who is also the Chief of Defence Forces (CDF), said this during a visit to Miranshah in North Waziristan district, the military's media wing said in a statement.

“He reaffirmed the unwavering resolve of the security forces, in close coordination with law enforcement agencies, to decisively eliminate the menace of terrorism and preserve the hard-earned peace and stability of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa,” the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said in a statement.
Mr. Munir also appreciated the KP police and expressed pride in its resilience and sacrifices against terrorism and Fitna-al-Khawarij.
The term Fitna-al-Khawarij is used by the federal government for the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan.

During the visit, the CDF was given a comprehensive briefing on “the prevailing security situation, ongoing intelligence-based operations [IBO] and measures being undertaken to consolidate the gains achieved through sustained counter-terrorism efforts, “ the ISPR statement said.
It added that CDF Munir also interacted with officers and troops and appreciated their “high level of preparedness, professionalism and unwavering commitment".
Security forces continue to carry out counterterrorism action in KP and Balochistan, the two provinces that have been particularly affected by terrorism in Pakistan.
On Saturday (November 14, 2026), ISPR said four troops, including a major, were killed while 24 terrorists were killed in IBOs in Balochistan and KP’s North Waziristan.
Furthermore, last week, 74 terrorists were killed in IBOs in KP and Balochistan.

The DKBA's Colonel Saw A One, responsible for security in the Three Pagodas Pass area in Karen State near the Thai border, was also designated by the U.S. on Thursday (November 19, 2026).
Jason Tower, senior expert at the Global Initiative Against Transnational Organized Crime, told that last week the Three Pagodas Pass region has been a "major expansion area" for scam compounds.

articles.title: Nepal PM Balendra Shah to visit India on November 22-23
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: In his first India visit, Nepal Prime Minister is expected to sign several MoUs and inaugurate projects
Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah will visit India on November 22-23, the Ministry of External Affairs announced on Friday (November 20, 2026).
Briefing the media in Kathmandu, Nepal’s Foreign Secretary Amrit Bahadur Rai said Mr. Shah will be accompanied by a 34-member delegation.

#WATCH | Kathmandu | "On the invitation of the Prime Minister of India, Nepali PM Balendra Shah will embark on a State visit to India from 22nd to 23rd November," says Nepal's Foreign Secretary Amrit Bahadur Rai. He adds, "It will be a 34-member government team that will depart from Kathmandu to New Delhi, India. During the visit, the Nepali PM will hold a delegation-level meeting on Monday with his Indian counterpart. Various projects relating to energy will be inaugurated by the two Prime Ministers. Various aspects of cooperation will be signed and exchanged. After the delegation-level talks, the two Prime Ministers will hold a joint press conference. Nepali PM will also call on the President of India, Droupadi Murmu. Nepali PM will also lay a wreath at Mahatma Gandhi's memorial at Rajghat. Nepali PM will also attend the Nepal-India Business Forum."

“Bilateral cooperation has witnessed progress across diverse sectors, including trade and commerce, development partnership, energy and water resources, and physical and digital connectivity, with growing engagement in newer areas such as start-ups, technology and innovation, and sports,” the Ministry said.

This will be the Nepal Prime Minister’s first visit to India since he took charge last March. Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle and Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal, who both visited India earlier this year, will join the delegation.
Official spokesperson for the Ministry of External Affairs Randhir Jaiswal said Mr. Shah’s trip will be a “state visit, during which he will be accorded state honours”.

“He will meet with our President and hold discussions with our Prime Minister. Given that this is a highly multifaceted relationship, the talks will cover a wide range of topics, including our development partnership, economic cooperation, and various other matters,” said Mr. Jaiswal during the biweekly media briefing on Friday (November 20, 2026).

Mr. Rai said the two countries are expected to sign several memorandums of understanding covering different areas of cooperation, and a few completed projects are expected to be inaugurated following PM Balendra Shah’s meeting with Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
Sources said the Dharchula Bridge, the land port of Banbasa at the Uttarakhand-Nepal border, and a train route between Janakpur and Gorakhpur are slated to be opened.

Earlier this month, India’s Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri visited Kathmandu. India’s External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar will be the first government representative to call on Prime Minister Shah upon his arrival on Sunday (November 22, 2026). Formal engagements will begin Monday morning with a ceremonial reception at the Rashtrapati Bhavan, followed by a visit to Rajghat, where Mr. Shah will lay a wreath at Mahatma Gandhi’s memorial. 🌐 International & Geopolitics 📅 20 Nov 2026 ⏱️ 4 Min Read

🎯 Exam Relevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy

In his first India visit, Nepal Prime Minister is expected to sign several MoUs and inaugurate projects

Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah will visit India on November 22-23, the Ministry of External Affairs announced on Friday (November 20, 2026).

Briefing the media in Kathmandu, Nepal’s Foreign Secretary Amrit Bahadur Rai said Mr. Shah will be accompanied by a 34-member delegation.

#WATCH | Kathmandu | "On the invitation of the Prime Minister of India, Nepali PM Balendra Shah will embark on a State visit to India from 22nd to 23rd November," says Nepal's Foreign Secretary Amrit Bahadur Rai. He adds, "It will be a 34-member government team that will depart from Kathmandu to New Delhi, India. During the visit, the Nepali PM will hold a delegation-level meeting on Monday with his Indian counterpart. Various projects relating to energy will be inaugurated by the two Prime Ministers. Various aspects of cooperation will be signed and exchanged. After the delegation-level talks, the two Prime Ministers will hold a joint press conference. Nepali PM will also call on the President of India, Droupadi Murmu. Nepali PM will also lay a wreath at Mahatma Gandhi's memorial at Rajghat. Nepali PM will also attend the Nepal-India Business Forum."

“Bilateral cooperation has witnessed progress across diverse sectors, including trade and commerce, development partnership, energy and water resources, and physical and digital connectivity, with growing engagement in newer areas such as start-ups, technology and innovation, and sports,” the Ministry said.

This will be the Nepal Prime Minister’s first visit to India since he took charge last March. Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle and Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal, who both visited India earlier this year, will join the delegation.

Official spokesperson for the Ministry of External Affairs Randhir Jaiswal said Mr. Shah’s trip will be a “state visit, during which he will be accorded state honours”.

“He will meet with our President and hold discussions with our Prime Minister. Given that this is a highly multifaceted relationship, the talks will cover a wide range of topics, including our development partnership, economic cooperation, and various other matters,” said Mr. Jaiswal during the biweekly media briefing on Friday (November 20, 2026).

Mr. Rai said the two countries are expected to sign several memorandums of understanding covering different areas of cooperation, and a few completed projects are expected to be inaugurated following PM Balendra Shah’s meeting with Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

Sources said the Dharchula Bridge, the land port of Banbasa at the Uttarakhand-Nepal border, and a train route between Janakpur and Gorakhpur are slated to be opened.

Earlier this month, India’s Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri visited Kathmandu. India’s External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar will be the first government representative to call on Prime Minister Shah upon his arrival on Sunday (November 22, 2026). Formal engagements will begin Monday morning with a ceremonial reception at the Rashtrapati Bhavan, followed by a visit to Rajghat, where Mr. Shah will lay a wreath at Mahatma Gandhi’s memorial. He will then meet Prime Minister Modi at Hyderabad House, where the MoUs will be signed. He will leave for Kathmandu later that afternoon.

articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Under the 2026 Float and Freeze option, candidates can carry forward their allotments without completing admission formalities, and even if their seats remain unchanged in Round 3, they can choose not to join; this flexibility has had significant implications in seat utilisation

Even as millions of candidates competed for admission, several undergraduate MBBS seats remained vacant during the NEET-UG 2026 counselling. Over 3,000-3,400 vacancies were reported after the initial All India Quota (AIQ) and State rounds, with approximately 410 seats still unfilled in deemed universities even after the Special Stray Vacancy Round.
(Sign up for THEdge , The Hindu’s weekly education newsletter.)

While government medical college seats were all filled, most remaining vacancies were in deemed universities. States such as Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karnataka accounted for a significant share of these vacancies, raising concerns about high fees, seat utilisation and equitable access to medical education.

As per the data published by the National Medical Commission (NMC), the total number of MBBS seats available in the country for the academic session 2026–27 stands at 1,40,664. Of these, 64,121 seats are available in government medical colleges, while the remaining 76,543 seats are in the private medical sector. The latter comprises 14,299 seats in deemed university medical colleges and 62,244 seats in self-financing private medical colleges. Thus, more than 54% of the total MBBS seats in the country are concentrated in the private medical sector, where the cost of medical education is generally substantially higher than in government institutions.

The National Testing Agency (NTA) reported that 11,21,185 candidates qualified NEET-UG 2026 by securing marks above the prescribed category-wise qualifying cut-off. This included 9,96,935 candidates belonging to the General/EWS qualifying category, and 1,24,250 candidates belonging to the OBC, SC and ST categories who qualified with scores ranging from 177 to 212 marks.

articles.title: Many imperatives: On India’s Asia diplomacy
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: India must shore up its partnerships in the Asian region

Each year, the summits of the 11-member Association of South-East Asian Nations mark an important moment on the diplomatic calendar: India is able to interact with all of its partners in the Indo-Pacific and engage global powers at the ASEAN-India Summit and the East Asia Summit. Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s talks with Indo-Pacific players focused on a future shaped “not by competition, but by cooperation”. This year, the summit in Manila hosted by the Philippines had many other imperatives. These were the first ASEAN summits since the U.S.-Israel attacks on Iran and Iran’s Hormuz blockade and strikes on Gulf countries that have upended energy and trade across South and South East Asia. Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s call for “peace, stability, and predictability” in the world during the EAS was aimed as much at leaders from the U.S., Russia and China as it was for the region. The visit had a bilateral context — the Philippines and India have intensified ties considerably in the past year, since the visit of President Bongbong Marcos to Delhi in August 2025, including the upgradation of the Strategic Partnership, maritime exchanges and negotiations over the supply of more Indian-made Brahmos missile battery systems to the Philippines. This year, after months of concerns about U.S. President Donald Trump’s lack of interest in the Quad grouping, the U.S. decided to host a summit of U.S.-India-Australia-Japan Quad leaders on the side-lines of the ASEAN summits, the first time the summit has been held in a non-Quad country.

Given the stakes, there were several outcomes from all the three summits that PM Modi attended back-to-back on Tuesday — the ASEAN India Summit launched a new cooperation on disaster management, and the East Asia Summit focused on countering cyber-crime. PM Modi’s announcement that India would give all ASEAN citizens free tourist visas is expected to increase people-to-people interactions and trade. At the Quad summit, President Trump made a number of announcements including the launch of a Quad Business leaders forum, to be held in Mumbai next year, and the first Quad naval exercises with patrol aircraft. However, the outcomes in Manila paled in significance to the anticipation over Mr. Trump’s next stop in Shenzhen for the Asia Pacific Economic Conference (APEC), with an unprecedented three-way summit with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping planned on Thursday. New Delhi must watch the outcomes of that summit among the “global superpowers” much more closely.
Editorial Context: Many imperatives: On India’s Asia diplomacy. This editorial examines the institutional, constitutional, and pragmatic dimensions shaping public policy and governance in India.

India must shore up its partnerships in the Asian region

Each year, the summits of the 11-member Association of South-East Asian Nations mark an important moment on the diplomatic calendar: India is able to interact with all of its partners in the Indo-Pacific and engage global powers at the ASEAN-India Summit and the East Asia Summit. Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s talks with Indo-Pacific players focused on a future shaped “not by competition, but by cooperation”. This year, the summit in Manila hosted by the Philippines had many other imperatives. These were the first ASEAN summits since the U.S.-Israel attacks on Iran and Iran’s Hormuz blockade and strikes on Gulf countries that have upended energy and trade across South and South East Asia. Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s call for “peace, stability, and predictability” in the world during the EAS was aimed as much at leaders from the U.S., Russia and China as it was for the region. The visit had a bilateral context — the Philippines and India have intensified ties considerably in the past year, since the visit of President Bongbong Marcos to Delhi in August 2025, including the upgradation of the Strategic Partnership, maritime exchanges and negotiations over the supply of more Indian-made Brahmos missile battery systems to the Philippines. This year, after months of concerns about U.S. President Donald Trump’s lack of interest in the Quad grouping, the U.S. decided to host a summit of U.S.-India-Australia-Japan Quad leaders on the side-lines of the ASEAN summits, the first time the summit has been held in a non-Quad country.

Given the stakes, there were several outcomes from all the three summits that PM Modi attended back-to-back on Tuesday — the ASEAN India Summit launched a new cooperation on disaster management, and the East Asia Summit focused on countering cyber-crime. PM Modi’s announcement that India would give all ASEAN citizens free tourist visas is expected to increase people-to-people interactions and trade. At the Quad summit, President Trump made a number of announcements including the launch of a Quad Business leaders forum, to be held in Mumbai next year, and the first Quad naval exercises with patrol aircraft. However, the outcomes in Manila paled in significance to the anticipation over Mr. Trump’s next stop in Shenzhen for the Asia Pacific Economic Conference (APEC), with an unprecedented three-way summit with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping planned on Thursday. New Delhi must watch the outcomes of that summit among the “global superpowers” much more closely.

articles.title: Testing times: On India’s two-Test series against New Zealand
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: India needs to be at its best in Tests against New Zealand

New Zealand at home remains an indomitable cricketing opposition. Even the great West Indian squad led by Clive Lloyd suffered a 0-1 Test series defeat in 1980. Pitches that look lush as English meadows, the wind that is often bone-chilling cold, and fast bowlers relishing their prospects, make any tour of New Zealand a difficult outing. So far, the visiting Indians have done well, having won the T20I and ODI series, but the real contest starts with the first Test at Wellington’s Basin Reserve from Thursday. The Shubman Gill-led men’s last overseas tour of Sri Lanka ended with a middling 1-0 victory in the two Tests, but more needs to be done against New Zealand in the latest two-Test series. Placed fourth in the ICC World Test Championship (WTC) table, and with hopes of securing a final berth seemingly fragile, India is in a win-all-games situation first up against New Zealand and later when Australia arrives next year. Against current WTC topper New Zealand, the Indian batters have to stay anchored. This is a line-up that no longer has Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli, Cheteshwar Pujara and Ajinkya Rahane. Gill and company get another opportunity to reiterate their credentials.

For some rugged inspiration they need not look beyond coach Gautam Gambhir in their dressing room. The doughty former India opener batted for 643 minutes while scoring a match-saving 137 in the Napier Test during the 2009 tour. The southpaw will be hoping that the current batting unit, which is high on flair, will remain sober and effectively counter the host. K.L. Rahul, Yashasvi Jaiswal, Devdutt Padikkal and Gill have the onerous task of negating the New Zealand seamers in their backyard. Rishabh Pant and Dhruv Jurel add depth, and if the former can successfully unleash his maverick batting approach, India can upset the host’s best-laid plans. New Zealand will miss the retired Kane Williamson but its batters would be comfortable on familiar surfaces. For India, much would hinge on how Jasprit Bumrah bowls. If the spearhead clicks, then it becomes easier for much of his support-cast that includes the persevering Mohammed Siraj, who was a touch rusty in Sri Lanka. From the squads of the past to the present unit, Ravindra Jadeja remains the link. Whether he will get a role to play or whether the management prefers an all-pace attack, remains a matter of conjecture. The home team led by Tom Latham will depend on Matt Henry, Kyle Jameson and other pacers, to choke the Indian batters. A hard task awaits India, first at Wellington and then at Christchurch.

articles.title: Madurai Bench of Madras High Court directs T.N. government not to open any new Tasmac shops
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: A Division Bench said the State already had a large number of Tasmac shops, and considering the public interest, new Tasmac shops should not be opened
The Madurai Bench of the Madras High Court on Wednesday directed the State government not to open any new Tasmac liquor shops in Tamil Nadu.
A Division Bench of Justices P. Velmurugan and K.K. Ramakrishnan said the State already had a large number of Tasmac shops, and considering the public interest, new Tasmac shops should not be opened.
The court passed the direction while allowing a public interest litigation petition filed by V. Manikandan of Navakinathupatti in Nallampillai village in Tiruchi district.

The petitioner said about 30 families lived in the village, where agriculture was the predominant occupation. The authorities had proposed to establish a Tasmac shop at Navakinathupatti. He said school students pass through the proposed site to reach the government school at Karattupatti, and that the area was accident-prone.
The opening of a liquor shop in the area would affect the safety of women and the welfare of school students, he said. He pointed out that a Tasmac shop was already located in a nearby village.
He said there was no necessity or justification for establishing another liquor shop in the vicinity without assessing the existing outlet’s impact.

The residents had already requested the authorities not to establish any liquor shop in the village or in the surrounding villages, he said, seeking a direction to restrain the authorities from establishing the Tasmac shop.
The petitioner said he had made a detailed representation to the authorities concerned in this regard. However, no action had been taken so far.

A Division Bench said the State already had a large number of Tasmac shops, and considering the public interest, new Tasmac shops should not be opened

The Madurai Bench of the Madras High Court on Wednesday directed the State government not to open any new Tasmac liquor shops in Tamil Nadu.

A Division Bench of Justices P. Velmurugan and K.K. Ramakrishnan said the State already had a large number of Tasmac shops, and considering the public interest, new Tasmac shops should not be opened.

The court passed the direction while allowing a public interest litigation petition filed by V. Manikandan of Navakinathupatti in Nallampillai village in Tiruchi district.

The petitioner said about 30 families lived in the village, where agriculture was the predominant occupation. The authorities had proposed to establish a Tasmac shop at Navakinathupatti. He said school students pass through the proposed site to reach the government school at Karattupatti, and that the area was accident-prone.

The opening of a liquor shop in the area would affect the safety of women and the welfare of school students, he said. He pointed out that a Tasmac shop was already located in a nearby village.

He said there was no necessity or justification for establishing another liquor shop in the vicinity without assessing the existing outlet’s impact.

The residents had already requested the authorities not to establish any liquor shop in the village or in the surrounding villages, he said, seeking a direction to restrain the authorities from establishing the Tasmac shop.

The petitioner said he had made a detailed representation to the authorities concerned in this regard. However, no action had been taken so far.

articles.title: BJP turns to Mathura temple issue amid cadre unease, allies’ pressure
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Political observers say the renewed focus on Krishna Janmabhoomi serves as a “smokescreen” to mask simmering discontent among the party cadre over the UGC’s equity rules, SIR drive and seat sharing with alliance partners

Days after Samajwadi Party (SP) chief Akhilesh Yadav made his ‘Dumdar Dalit’ outreach in Agra, the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) responded on November 16 with ‘Radhe Radhe, Kamal Khila De’ and ‘Abki Baari Baanke Bihari’.

It was senior BJP leader and Deputy Chief Minister Keshav Prasad Maurya who spelt out to reporters, during the party’s two-day conclave in Mathura earlier this week, that constructing a grand temple at the Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi in Mathura would be at the centre of their campaign for the upcoming Uttar Pradesh Assembly election. articles.title: Cyclone 'Akvan' updates: Akvan likely to cross between Machilipatnam and Puri, says APSDMA
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The storm picked up speed to 7 kmph over the past six hours. It was about 580 km from Visakhapatnam, 590 km from Machilipatnam and 710 km from Gopalpur in Odisha

Odisha Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi said around 50,000 people have so far been evacuated to safety ahead of the likely landfall of severe cyclonic storm ‘Akvan’ between Narsapur in Andhra Pradesh and Puri in the eastern state.

Mr. Majhi, who presided over a high-level review meeting on the preparedness of the state government, said the highest number of people will be evacuated from Ganjam district and the process is underway.
“Our target is zero casualties and the evacuation drive has been launched in a massive manner, both in the plains and hilly terrain,” he said.

The Odisha government on Wednesday placed eight districts on high alert as severe cyclonic storm Akvan , brewing over the west-central and adjoining central parts of the south Bay of Bengal, is forecast to trigger extremely heavy rainfall in the State over the next two days. Odisha puts eight districts on high alert as severe cyclonic storm Akvan advances towards coast Odisha declares eight districts on high alert as Cyclone Akvan nears, cancels leave, evacuations underway, and IAS-led emergency operations activated.
Odisha declares eight districts on high alert as Cyclone Akvan nears, cancels leave, evacuations underway, and IAS-led emergency operations activated.

On Cyclone Akvan, IMD DG Mrutyunjay Mohapatra says, “It will hit between Narsapur and Puri, the coasts of North Andhra Pradesh and South Odisha, by the afternoon of 20th November. At that time, its wind speed is likely to be between 90-100 kmph gusting to 110 kmph”

articles.title: UEF, IIT-M join hands for Tamil Nadu Growth Conclave 2026; focus on 10 key sectors
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The United Economic Forum (UEF) Chamber of Commerce has signed an MoU with the Indian Institute of Technology - Madras (IIT-M) to collaborate for the Tamil Nadu Growth Conclave 2026 scheduled to be held on December 8, 2026. The objective of this MoU is to facilitate knowledge sharing, industry academia collaboration, innovation, investment and stakeholder engagement towards Tamil Nadu’s economic growth.

The event will focus on 10 sectors, including Automotive & EV; Electronics & Semiconductors; IT, AI and Digital; Advanced Engineering & Capital Goods; Textiles & Technical Textiles; Pharma, Biotech & MedTech; Agri & Food Processing; Renewable & Green Energy; Logistics, Ports & Global Trade and Aerospace & Defence. Professors from the IIT-M ecosystem will lead each of these sectors.

V.Kamakoti, IIT-Madras Director through a video message said: “IIT Madras, and IIT Madras Research Park, and all our ecosystem are very happy to be associated with UEF to launch this Tamil Nadu Conclave 2026 as we march towards a multi-trillion economy.”

Mr. Kamakoti further said: “There are 10 highly emerging and extremely important from a societal angle verticals that have been identified, all the way from automotive, EV, electronics, semiconductor, IT, AI, technical, textiles, pharma, agri, renewable, green energy, aerospace, defense, logistics, and advanced engineering and capital goods.” He added, “And in each of these verticals, we are going to talk not just about the products, but also the supply chain, the logistics that is involved, the raw materials that are involved to make these, because many of them are deep tech technologies.”

Jinnah Rafiq Ahmed, Chairman, UEF – Tamil Nadu Growth Conclave 2026 and Executive Chairman and Managing Director, Kothari Industrial Corporation Limited (KICL), said that a few MoUs would be inked at the conclave. To a query on whether investments are moving out of Tamil Nadu, he said that a lot of companies want to come to Tamil Nadu.

“Tamil Nadu’s industrial growth will be there, will continue and it will be unimaginable. Definitely, Tamil Nadu’s industrial growth will be very aggressive in the coming years. An industry from Tamil Nadu going out of State will not happen. And if it is, it might be an additional project in other States,” he said.

Ahmed A. R. Buhari, President — United Economic Forum (UEF) said, “Tamil Nadu has set an ambitious target of becoming a $1.5 trillion economy by 2036. UEF’s Unnatha Tamizhagam vision aspires to contribute towards Tamil Nadu becoming a $4 trillion economy by 2047.” The United Economic Forum in association with Kothari Industrial Corporation Limited and Airtel Business is organising the Tamil Nadu Growth Conclave 2026.

articles.title: U.S., Venezuela sign deal to re-establish military ties: Hegseth
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The U.S. Defence Secretary said that following the January capture of Nicolas Maduro by the U.S. military, the country “has gone from our most aggressive regional threat to a compliant security partner”
Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, speaking in Venezuela, said the two countries have signed an agreement to re-establish military ties, from training to intelligence sharing.

Mr. Hegseth said that following the January capture of Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro by the U.S. military, the country “has gone from our most aggressive regional threat to a compliant security partner.”
Mr. Hegseth also praised the “close cooperation” with interim President Delcy Rodriguez that allowed officials “to stabilise Venezuela and rid it of narco-terrorists once and for all.”
The Pentagon did not immediately offer further details on the new partnership.

Ms. Rodríguez separately lauded the opportunity to strengthen the military partnership. “I hope that this technical-military cooperation … can be brought to its highest possible level so that ... we may address common threats,” she said.
Mr. Hegseth’s visit underscores efforts by President Donald Trump’s administration to deepen its influence in the South American country since U.S. forces ousted Maduro in January.

Mr. Hegseth is the latest member of Mr. Trump’s Cabinet to travel to Venezuela following visits this year by the Interior and Energy secretaries, who have focused on efforts to tap its oil reserves and critical minerals. Mr. Trump said in August that Mr. Hegseth helped broker a sweeping deal for the U.S. to take control of some Venezuelan oil reserves.
The head of U.S. military operations in Latin America, Gen. Francis Donovan of U.S. Southern Command, also has met interim authorities in Venezuela at least twice this year.

The U.S. military has been expanding its attention on the region since Mr. Trump returned to the White House last year, with the Republican president promising to focus more on the Western Hemisphere and battle Latin American drug cartels.

To try to stem the flow of narcotics into the U.S. and the scourge of fatal overdoses, American forces have been attacking what the Trump administration says are boats smuggling drugs in the Caribbean Sea and the eastern Pacific Ocean. At least 240 people have been killed since the administration began targeting those it calls “narcoterrorists” in September 2025, although U.S. officials have released little evidence publicly to support claims the vessels were carrying drugs.

articles.title: Climate promises need to become praxis

fullParagraphs: The world does not lack climate declarations. They simply do not have the speed, resources, and cooperation required to make them a reality

They also called for the mobilisation of $1.3 trillion a year from public and private sectors. While these commitments acknowledge that there is a need for vulnerable countries to receive more support, the true test is whether the funds are delivered on time to countries at affordable prices and in a usable format.

articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: On the occasion of Akshaya Navami, State Agriculture Minister Sinha spoke about connecting five pledges with culture, nature, and farmers

Bihar Agriculture Minister and senior Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leader Vijay Kumar Sinha pledged on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) to “connect every family of Bihar with nature, medicinal and fruit‑bearing plants, community farming, promotion of farmers and agriculture‑based industry, and protection of traditions based on culture and agriculture.”

Mr. Sinha also pledged to make Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s campaign of “Ek Ped, Maa ke Naam” (one tree in one’s mother’s name) a people’s movement. PM Modi is scheduled to visit Bihar on November 21 to inaugurate and lay the foundation stones of several projects.

On the occasion of Akshaya Navami, Mr. Sinha spoke about connecting five pledges with culture, nature, and farmers. “Every family in the state will be connected with nature, medicinal and fruit-bearing plants, community farming, promotion of farmers, agriculture-based industry, and the protection of traditions rooted in culture and agriculture,” Mr. Sinha, who was also Deputy Chief Minister in the previous NDA government, told media persons on Wednesday (November 18, 2026).

“If nature is saved, humanity will smile, and it is greenery that will eventually bring happiness to the earth,” he said, adding, “this initiative started by us would become a new base for a people’s movement by connecting nature, farmers, and agriculture together.”
The Agriculture Minister appealed to people to plant at least “one fruit-bearing and medicinal plant to secure life and the future of the coming generation”.

“It is our responsibility to offer a clean and green environment to our future generation,” he asserted. He also put focus on connecting our festivals, agriculture and culture with nature and cited an example of the recently concluded biggest four-day Chhath (Sun God offering) festival.
The Agriculture Minister mentioned the names of several traditional trees and said “our forefathers had created a way of environmental protection through our religious faith”.
“Now the time has come for farmers to return to natural farming and offer pure and healthy food stuffs to the coming generation,” he appealed further.

articles.title: Police, magistrates, and sessions judges cannot refuse bail if offences are bailable: Madras High Court
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Justice N. Ramesh says they do not enjoy any discretion to deny bail in such cases and orders circulation of his verdict to all judicial officers in Tamil Nadu and Puducherry

Expressing shock over a case where a metropolitan magistrate and a sessions judge in Chennai had denied bail in a case booked for bailable offences, the Madras High Court has reminded judicial officers in Tamil Nadu and Puducherry that they do not enjoy any such discretion.

Justice N. Ramesh held that even if the accused had mentioned a wrong provision of the law under which they had sought bail, it would be the duty of the judicial officers to find out whether the offences for which the petitioners had been arrested were bailable or not, and then take an appropriate decision.

“If the offences are bailable and the accused is prepared to give bail, he shall be released under Section 478(1) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS). The police officer, the magistrate, the court of session, or this court would have no discretion to refuse,” the judge wrote.

The judge made it clear that the gravity of an accusation, the stage of investigation, an awaited forensic report, antecedents of the petitioner, or the apprehension of absconding or tampering with evidence could be cited as grounds only for denying bail in non-bailable offences and not in cases related to bailable offences.

Further, while granting bail for bailable offences, “the court may fix the amount of the bond and decide whether sureties are required. It may not attach any other condition. An accused who is indigent, or who is unable to give a bail bond within a week of his arrest, must be released on his own bond,” the judge added.

Justice Ramesh further made it clear that a bail granted in respect of bailable offences could be cancelled only by the High Court if the conduct of the accused, after his release, was found to be prejudicial to a fair trial. He also said that if a person had violated the conditions of a bail bond in some case, then he could be denied bail in the next case even if the offences in the subsequent case were bailable.

The judge pointed out that the BNSS, as well as special legislations related to criminal offences, clearly specify the list of offences, such as those which carry a maximum punishment of three years, which were bailable, and those which were non-bailable.

He directed the High Court’s Registrar General Deepthi Arivunithi to circulate a copy of his order to all Principal District and Sessions Judges and the Chief Judicial Magistrates in Tamil Nadu and Puducherry so that it could be brought to the notice of judicial officers across the State and the Union Territory. A copy should also be sent to the Director of the Tamil Nadu State Judicial Academy, the judge said.

The orders were passed while granting bail to P. Rajagopal of Thiruvanmiyur in Chennai, who was arrested by the Chennai Cyber Crime police on October 22, 2026, for having posted an obscene, abusive, and derogatory remark against Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay on the X handle of the accused on June 12, 2026.

The petitioner was booked under Sections 296(b) (using abusive words) of the BNSS and 67 of the Information Technology Act, 2000. However, there was nothing on record to show that the police had informed the accused that both the provisions were bailable, the judge said.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity 📅 19 Nov 2026 ⏱️ 4 Min Read

📰 Police, magistrates, and sessions judges cannot refuse bail if offences are bailable: Madras High Court

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
🔮 Futuristic Word Radar: Paragraph ke kisi bhi English word par Double-Click karein — turant uska Hinglish Meaning + Picture screen par dekhein!

Justice N. Ramesh says they do not enjoy any discretion to deny bail in such cases and orders circulation of his verdict to all judicial officers in Tamil Nadu and Puducherry

Expressing shock over a case where a metropolitan magistrate and a sessions judge in Chennai had denied bail in a case booked for bailable offences, the Madras High Court has reminded judicial officers in Tamil Nadu and Puducherry that they do not enjoy any such discretion.

Justice N. Ramesh held that even if the accused had mentioned a wrong provision of the law under which they had sought bail, it would be the duty of the judicial officers to find out whether the offences for which the petitioners had been arrested were bailable or not, and then take an appropriate decision.

“If the offences are bailable and the accused is prepared to give bail, he shall be released under Section 478(1) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS). The police officer, the magistrate, the court of session, or this court would have no discretion to refuse,” the judge wrote.

The judge made it clear that the gravity of an accusation, the stage of investigation, an awaited forensic report, antecedents of the petitioner, or the apprehension of absconding or tampering with evidence could be cited as grounds only for denying bail in non-bailable offences and not in cases related to bailable offences.

Further, while granting bail for bailable offences, “the court may fix the amount of the bond and decide whether sureties are required. It may not attach any other condition. An accused who is indigent, or who is unable to give a bail bond within a week of his arrest, must be released on his own bond,” the judge added.

Justice Ramesh further made it clear that a bail granted in respect of bailable offences could be cancelled only by the High Court if the conduct of the accused, after his release, was found to be prejudicial to a fair trial. He also said that if a person had violated the conditions of a bail bond in some case, then he could be denied bail in the next case even if the offences in the subsequent case were bailable.

The judge pointed out that the BNSS, as well as special legislations related to criminal offences, clearly specify the list of offences, such as those which carry a maximum punishment of three years, which were bailable, and those which were non-bailable.

He directed the High Court’s Registrar General Deepthi Arivunithi to circulate a copy of his order to all Principal District and Sessions Judges and the Chief Judicial Magistrates in Tamil Nadu and Puducherry so that it could be brought to the notice of judicial officers across the State and the Union Territory. A copy should also be sent to the Director of the Tamil Nadu State Judicial Academy, the judge said.

The orders were passed while granting bail to P. Rajagopal of Thiruvanmiyur in Chennai, who was arrested by the Chennai Cyber Crime police on October 22, 2026, for having posted an obscene, abusive, and derogatory remark against Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay on the X handle of the accused on June 12, 2026.

The petitioner was booked under Sections 296(b) (using abusive words) of the BNSS and 67 of the Information Technology Act, 2000. However, there was nothing on record to show that the police had informed the accused that both the provisions were bailable, the judge said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The petitioner was booked under Sections 296(b) (using abusive words) of the BNSS and 67 of the Information Technology Act, 2000. However, there was nothing on record to show that the police had informed the accused that both the provisions were bailable, the judge said.

articles.title: TVK MLA V.S. Babu, who defeated M.K. Stalin in Kolathur, passes away
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam MLA V.S. Babu had been admitted to MGM Healthcare in Aminjikarai, Chennai, with a prolonged respiratory illness

Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) MLA V.S. Babu, who defeated DMK president and former Chief Minister M.K. Stalin in the Kolathur Assembly constituency in the 2026 Tamil Nadu Assembly election, died following a cardiac arrest on Thursday (November 19, 2026). He was 75.

Mr. Babu was admitted to MGM Hospital in Aminjikarai, Chennai, on September 9 with a respiratory illness. According to the medical bulletin issued by the hospital, he was under intensive care. His condition continued to deteriorate, and he subsequently suffered a cardiac arrest and died on November 19 at 2.24 p.m.
Mr. Babu started his political career in the DMK as an area secretary and went on to become the party’s north Chennai district secretary.

He was first elected to the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly from the Purasawalkam Assembly constituency in the 2006 Assembly election as a DMK candidate. Following the 2008 delimitation exercise, the Purasawalkam constituency ceased to exist, and many areas falling under it became part of the newly formed Kolathur Assembly constituency.

Mr. Babu, then a local face of the DMK, reportedly played a considerable role in Mr. Stalin’s victory in the Kolathur Assembly constituency in the 2011 election. After 2011, Mr. Babu stayed away from politics for a while before joining the AIADMK in 2016. Earlier this year, he joined the TVK in the presence of party president and now Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay.
With his passing, the number of vacancies in the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly has risen to six.

Tamil Nadu Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar condoled the death of Mr. Babu. In a post on X, Lok Bhavan, Tamil Nadu, said the Governor remembers the departed leader’s public life and service and prays to the almighty to grant strength and courage to the bereaved family to bear this irreparable loss.

In his condolence message, Mr. Vijay said Mr. Babu dedicated himself wholeheartedly to public life, earning the love, support, and trust of people. His death is an irreparable loss, said Mr. Vijay, extending sympathies to his family members and people of the Kolathur Assembly segment.

Mr. Stalin, in a post on X, expressed shock over demise of Mr. Babu and extended condolences to his family members. Ministers of Tamil Nadu government, PMK president Anbumani Ramadoss, BJP State president Nainar Nagenthran, We The Leaders founder K. Annamalai, and Manithaneya Makkal Katchi leader M.H. Jawahirullah also condoled his death.

articles.title: BJP mocks Rahul Gandhi's U.S. remarks, says AI can predict his speeches
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The BJP also said that Congress should consider sending an AI-generated version of its leader abroad because he keeps repeating the same words

The BJP on Thursday (November 19, 2026) slammed Congress leader Rahul Gandhi for his remarks during his U.S. visit, accusing him of making “Hawai” allegations about India's electoral process and lowering the country's image on foreign soil.
The BJP also said that Congress should consider sending an AI-generated version of its leader abroad because he keeps repeating the same words.

Interacting with students at the University of Chicago on Wednesday (November 18, 2026), Mr. Gandhi said Indian democracy is “sacred”, and the Congress is ready to face electoral defeats until people realise that the system has been “completely demolished”.
Mr. Gandhi also said that boycotting elections over alleged flaws in the system would bring an end to Indian democracy, which the Congress does not intend to do.

Addressing a press conference at the party headquarters, BJP spokesperson and Rajya Sabha MP Sudhanshu Trivedi said it is unfortunate that Mr. Gandhi is making remarks against India in Chicago, the city where Swami Vivekananda had once brought glory to the country.
“Today, we have a leader of the opposition who is lowering the prestige of Mother India at the same place. This is unfortunate for the Congress and painful for Indians,” Mr. Trivedi said.
ALSO WATCH Watch: India facing ‘economic disaster’: Rahul Gandhi at Columbia university
He was responding to Mr. Gandhi's remarks questioning the 2024 Lok Sabha elections and concerns over electoral irregularities.

Referring to Mr. Gandhi's claim that a Brazilian model voted “23 times” in India, Mr. Trivedi questioned the basis of the charge. “Anyone coming from abroad should have an immigration record, shouldn't they? Just imagine, a leader of the opposition can make such ‘Hawai’ allegations,” he said.
Taking a swipe at Mr. Gandhi's frequent foreign visits, Mr. Trivedi said the Congress should stop spending money on sending him abroad.

fullParagraphs: While also highlighting the economic progress India has made over the course of his tenure as Prime Minister, Mr. Modi also pointed out several ways in which the private sector needed to improve

Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday (November 19, 2026) tore into gathered industry leaders on a variety of issues, including their lack of progress since the times of Mahatma Gandhi towards manufacturing in India, companies’ failures to increase employment and wages, the trend of exporters sending their highest quality items out of the country, and industry’s lack of preparedness to exploit benefits unleashed by Free Trade Agreements (FTAs).

While addressing the inaugural session of FICCI’s Annual General Meeting in Delhi, Mr. Modi also spoke about the various strengths of the economy, including its move from a ‘fragile five’ economy to the fastest-growing major economy in the world, the increase in per capita income, and the World Bank’s recognition of India’s poverty reduction efforts.
However, he also voiced several points of criticism against the Indian private sector. One of these had to do with the Make in India mission and the attempt to make India self reliant.
“In 1930, Gandhi came to you and said exactly this,” Mr. Modi said. “And even today, after all these years, I have to say the same thing. Is this your success or your failure?”

articles.title: Indian democracy 'sacred', boycotting polls will end it: Rahul Gandhi at University of Chicago
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: “So, our strategy is to expose what is going on and take the beating until the people of India realise that the system has been fully demolished,” the Congress leader said

Indian democracy is "sacred" and the Congress is ready to face electoral defeats until people realise that the system has been completely demolished, Leader of the Opposition (LoP) in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi said.

Interacting with students at the University of Chicago on Wednesday (November 18, 2026), Mr. Gandhi said boycotting elections over alleged flaws in the electoral system would bring an end to Indian democracy, and the Congress party does not intend to do that.

"Indian democracy is sacred. For me to even say that there is a problem in Indian democracy is difficult without 100, 200, 300 per cent proof," he said during the interaction moderated by Prof Robert Pape.
The Congress leader said asking the opposition to boycott elections would end democracy that very minute.

"But what happens to all the opposition workers if we tell them, 'Okay, don't participate in the election?' If we say that we are not going to contest elections, we end Indian democracy that minute. And we don't want to end the structure of Indian democracy,” Mr. Gandhi said.
“So, our strategy is to expose what is going on and take the beating until the people of India realise that the system has been fully demolished,” he said.

Mr. Gandhi was on a two-day visit to the U.S. during which he interacted with the students of Columbia University in New York on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) and the University of Chicago on Wednesday (November 18, 2026).

“In another life, Jensen Huang might have been a teacher,” says Tae Kim in his book The Nvidia Way . Whether he likes it or not, the Nvidia co-founder’s reality has now been reset, forcing him back to his idiosyncratic style of solving problems: diagramming on a whiteboard. But this time he won’t get a clean start as the scandal-hit former chief of Nvidia will face intense scrutiny over his affair with a Chinese businesswoman who is at the centre of an alleged spy scandal.

Within days of reports emerging about Mr. Huang’s affair with Alice Huang , The New York Times reported a second relationship, with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s head of healthcare and one of his direct reports. By then, the controversy had come to a head, forcing Mr. Huang to resign as CEO of Nvidia, the company he had built from scratch.

articles.title: Japanese PM Takaichi calls for continued dialogue with China to ease bilateral tensions
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Earlier in the day, Ms. Takaichi shook hands with Chinese President Xi Jinping and later held a meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin

Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi on Thursday (November 19, 2026) called for continued dialogue and communication with China to ease bilateral tensions triggered by her remarks on Taiwan, saying Beijing is an "important neighbour" with which Tokyo has several outstanding issues.
Ms. Takaichi is in Shenzhen to attend the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting.

"China is an important neighbour, and between the two countries there are outstanding issues, and that is why it is important to continue communicating and having dialogue,” she told the media on the sidelines of the APEC summit.
Earlier in the day, Ms. Takaichi shook hands with Chinese President Xi Jinping and later held a meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin.
When asked about her brief interaction with Mr. Xi, the Japanese PM said she thanked him for the invitation and congratulated him on successfully hosting the APEC summit.

Relations between Tokyo and Beijing have sharply deteriorated after Takaichi told parliament in November last year that a Chinese attack on Taiwan, a self-governed island claimed by China, could trigger a situation in which Japan's Self-Defence Forces might support US forces.
Her remarks infuriated China, prompting it to take a series of political and economic measures against Japan, including export restrictions on rare earths used in a wide range of high-tech products.
Asked about the controversy, Ms. Takaichi said Japan's four political documents governing its relations with China remained unchanged and continued to serve as the foundation of bilateral ties.

Tokyo will continue to advance a comprehensive strategic relationship of mutual benefit with Beijing while pursuing dialogue to protect their respective national interests and build constructive and stable ties, she said, according to the Hong Kong-based South China Morning Post.
Ms. Takaichi refrained from commenting on a hypothetical Taiwan contingency, saying Japan's position on Taiwan, as articulated in the 1972 Japan-China Joint Communique, remained unchanged.

articles.title: Xi-Trump-Putin trilateral meeting LIVE: Xi-Trump-Putin summit begins in China; no peace ever forged by declining opportunities, says Trump
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: China-U.S. relations 'stable and improved', Xi says; Ukraine strikes Crimean bridge again as Trump says U.S., China want to help end war

Some in the West are comparing the three-way meeting to the 1945 Yalta conference, where the wartime leaders of the U.S., Britain and the Soviet Union divided Germany and Berlin, carved out zones of influence in Europe, and agreed to establish the United Nations.
The Kremlin, which long has courted the concept of a “multipolar world” offering an equal say to all nations, plays down the Yalta comparisons, which are also unwelcome to China for similar reasons.

Fyodor Lukyanov, a pro-Kremlin foreign policy expert, noted that even as Moscow publicly rejects the Yalta analogy, it seems to believe the leaders could “reach agreements and make decisions that will determine global developments”.
Of the three nations, “it seems that only Russia really believes in the possibility of global control”, he told a recent roundtable.

Chatham House director Bronwen Maddox said in a commentary that “standing with Xi and Trump, Putin will look like one of the three main leaders of the world”, even though “Russia is no superpower” and its economy, overloaded with military spending, is dwindling.
She warned that “the danger for Ukraine is that Trump uses this summit to try to advance his notion of peace, including giving Russia territory it has not managed to seize by force”.

The meeting follows US-mediated peace talks between Russia and Ukraine held in Abu Dhabi last week for the first time in nine months. The negotiations produced few visible results as the parties stuck to their sharply divergent demands. -- AP
Trilateral Xi-Putin-Trump summit draws Yalta 1945 comparisons, highlighting postwar order shifts amid Ukraine tensions and multipolar world debates.
An unprecedented summit in China between the presidents of China, the United States and Russia ended on Thursday (November 19, 2026) after around an hour and 20 minutes.
U.S. President Donald Trump immediately left in his motorcade from the Kylin Villa venue towards Shenzhen’s airport after the talks with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin.- AFP

articles.title: U.S. court orders delivery of summonses to Doval, Goel through Delhi courts
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Citing the Hague Conventions and relevant provisions of the Indian Code of Civil Procedure (CPC), a U.S. federal court Judge Katherine Polk Failla said foreign courts can serve summonses to Mr. Doval and Mr. Goel through Indian courts

A U.S. federal court has ordered the delivery of summonses to National Security Advisor Ajit Doval and former Research and Analysis Wing chief Samant Goel through Delhi courts in connection with a lawsuit filed by Khalistani separatist Gurpatwant Singh Pannun.
Mr. Pannun is wanted by Indian probe agencies on various terror charges.

In an order dated November 13, the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York directed its clerk to send the summonses and accompanying judicial documents to the Patiala House District Court for Mr. Doval, and the Dwarka and Tis Hazari district courts for Mr. Goel.

"The court respectfully requests the assistance of receiving Indian courts in effecting service of process upon the defendants in this civil action pending before this court," says an order by Judge Katherine Polk Failla.
Citing the Hague Conventions and relevant provisions of the Indian Code of Civil Procedure (CPC), Ms. Failla said foreign courts can serve summonses to Mr. Doval and Mr. Goel through Indian courts.
The CPC permits summonses issued by foreign civil courts notified by the central government to be transmitted to Indian courts and served in the same manner as summonses issued by domestic courts.
The U.S. court order stated that the standard procedure for serving the summonses through India's central authority under the Hague Convention had been attempted but rejected.
The court subsequently authorised an alternative mode of service under Article 19 of the convention and the relevant provisions of India's CPC.
Mr. Pannun, a U.S.-based legal counsel for the banned organisation Sikhs for Justice (SFJ), has filed the civil lawsuit seeking damages over an alleged attempt on his life.
He has accused Mr. Doval of orchestrating the alleged assassination plot with the involvement of India's external intelligence agency RAW.
