Citing the Hague Conventions and relevant provisions of the Indian Code of Civil Procedure (CPC), a U.S. federal court Judge Katherine Polk Failla said foreign courts can serve summonses to Mr. Doval and Mr. Goel through Indian courts

A U.S. federal court has ordered the delivery of summonses to National Security Advisor Ajit Doval and former Research and Analysis Wing chief Samant Goel through Delhi courts in connection with a lawsuit filed by Khalistani separatist Gurpatwant Singh Pannun.

Mr. Pannun is wanted by Indian probe agencies on various terror charges.

In an order dated November 13, the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York directed its clerk to send the summonses and accompanying judicial documents to the Patiala House District Court for Mr. Doval, and the Dwarka and Tis Hazari district courts for Mr. Goel.

"The court respectfully requests the assistance of receiving Indian courts in effecting service of process upon the defendants in this civil action pending before this court," says an order by Judge Katherine Polk Failla.

Citing the Hague Conventions and relevant provisions of the Indian Code of Civil Procedure (CPC), Ms. Failla said foreign courts can serve summonses to Mr. Doval and Mr. Goel through Indian courts.

The CPC permits summonses issued by foreign civil courts notified by the central government to be transmitted to Indian courts and served in the same manner as summonses issued by domestic courts.

The U.S. court order stated that the standard procedure for serving the summonses through India's central authority under the Hague Convention had been attempted but rejected.

The court subsequently authorised an alternative mode of service under Article 19 of the convention and the relevant provisions of India's CPC.

Mr. Pannun, a U.S.-based legal counsel for the banned organisation Sikhs for Justice (SFJ), has filed the civil lawsuit seeking damages over an alleged attempt on his life.

He has accused Mr. Doval of orchestrating the alleged assassination plot with the involvement of India's external intelligence agency RAW.

articles.title: Musk says he feels 'pretty foolish' for failed U.S. election spending
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: World's richest man Elon Musk said on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) he felt "pretty foolish" for donating nearly half a billion dollars to failed campaigns in recent U.S. midterm elections, backing right-wing Republicans in races that were largely won by Democrats.

"I feel pretty foolish about having spent so much money and not seeing much for it, or maybe it would have been much worse without that," Mr. Musk said via videolink at the New York Times Dealbook conference.
ALSO WATCH Trump’s political future, MAGA and the Democrats | Neera Tanden interview
Mr. Musk said his goal was "either the presidency, the House or the Senate be of the other party. That was my actual goal here, which failed by the way."
The Tesla and SpaceX boss sought to extract a lesson from the folly, telling the audience: "It certainly shows that American elections are not just about money."
"Obviously you can put a lot of money into election and have an effect that is relatively minor, and I think that was the case here," he continued.
The midterms weren't the South Africa-born tech tycoon's first foray into American elections.

Mr. Musk spent more than $250 million to help U.S. President Donald Trump return to the White House for his second term and briefly led the 80-year-old Republican's Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE), before they had a public falling out.
They've since reconciled and instead of souring on Republican politics, Mr. Musk has continued to back Republicans who the President champions.

Among the candidates he backed most strongly was Texas Senate candidate Ken Paxton, with Mr. Musk contributing an estimated $220 million to the Republican, only for the race to be won by James Talarico, a 37-year-old Democrat.

articles.title: GTA VI is here, and India has taken the day off
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Grand Theft Auto VI is a homecoming, and this time a good part of the city was built in Bengaluru

This week, Grand Theft Auto VI landed on Blinkit, in a collectible box available in select areas across 11 cities. There is no disc inside, only a download code, because Rockstar is selling the game purely as a download, even in stores. That makes for instant gratification of a new kind: the most anticipated game in years can now reach your doorstep in minutes, about as quickly as a loaf of bread, with the code ready to redeem the moment it arrives. Blinkit co-founder Albinder Dhindsa announced the offering on X on November 18, noting that it had taken 13 years for the game to arrive. It is a very 2026 way to launch a game, and an apt one, given that Grand Theft Auto has always found its way to Indian players through whichever door happened to be open.

The game itself costs ₹5,999 for the Standard Edition and ₹7,499 for the Ultimate Edition on both PlayStation and Xbox, which is almost exactly double what Grand Theft Auto V cost here at launch. In dollars, though, Indian buyers pay about US$63 for the Standard Edition versus the $79.99 charged in the United States, and pre-order customers also receive the Vintage Vice City Pack. It is on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S only for now, with no PC version announced, which is a shift for a series so many Indians first met on a computer, though Grand Theft Auto V took the same route and reached PC in 2015.

GTA 6 is now live on Blinkit! 🎮 It took 13 years for GTA 6 to be released. In the meantime, we built Blinkit so that you can get the game delivered in minutes. We've launched it in select areas of Delhi, Gurugram, Faridabad, Ghaziabad, Noida, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Mumbai, Pune, Kolkata & Ahmedabad (launching in more cities between today and tomorrow). We'll deliver a physical box with a download code inside (the box is a nice collectible for your shelf). Get yours now and start downloading so you're ready to play from 19th November. Expecting a suspicious number of sick leaves over the next few days 😮‍💨

In solidarity, consumer electronics brand boAt offered employees an optional day off on November 19, announcing it with the caption Out of office. Into Vice City. In Chennai, interior design firm Inde by ChairsCarte declared a holiday for its staff, interns and freelancers, calling it “just a day off for a game we’ve waited years for”.

For a generation of Indian players, the first port of call was the neighbourhood cyber café. Vice City and San Andreas, which defined the series in the early 2000s, were among the first open worlds many Indians explored, playing on rented computers by the hour, often between rounds of Counter-Strike, long before gaming became a career in India. San Andreas also gave us cheat codes, strings of nonsense such as HESOYAM, which replenished health, armour and cash in one go. For those who grew up typing them, they remain shorthand for nostalgia.

Even Indians who have never owned a copy know the series, thanks to its meme culture. The grey-and-red Wasted screen from GTA V, which appears when a character dies, has spent years slapped onto videos of people and animals spectacularly failing at something. Big Smoke’s exasperated yell at CJ for losing a train in San Andreas became so widely shared that Rockstar later named a GTA V trophy Better Than CJ in its honour. But the longest-running joke was about the wait. As the sequel failed to materialise, “We got X before GTA 6” became the Internet’s way of reacting to anything improbable. India took to it enthusiastically, with electronics retailer Croma fuelling another round when the game was delayed to November 19, 2026.
Your KRA is updated to completing missions and side quests 🎮 https://t.co/x1xSmUIPqU

Grand Theft Auto V arrived in India in September 2013, priced at around ₹3,000 for the PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360. But its second life here began after PUBG Mobile was banned in September 2020. Several of India’s biggest streamers, including Dynamo and MortaL, turned to other games, GTA V among them, and roleplay helped make it a mainstay of Indian livestreaming.

A roleplay server is a fan-run version of GTA V’s online world where players invent characters with names, jobs and backstories, from cab drivers and paramedics to cops and small-time crooks, and inhabit them for hours. Soulcity, launched by S8UL and Velocity Gaming in early 2023, became one of India’s biggest GTA V roleplay servers and helped create a new breed of gaming star. S8UL co-founder Lokesh Jain, better known as 8Bit Goldy, played a character called Rocket Singh on the server. The scene grew big enough for S8UL to sign creators such as Sunny Jha, aka Pitaji Playz, specifically for its GTA roleplay roster.

📰 GTA VI is here, and India has taken the day off

🎯 Exam Relevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action

Grand Theft Auto VI is a homecoming, and this time a good part of the city was built in Bengaluru

This week, Grand Theft Auto VI landed on Blinkit, in a collectible box available in select areas across 11 cities. There is no disc inside, only a download code, because Rockstar is selling the game purely as a download, even in stores. That makes for instant gratification of a new kind: the most anticipated game in years can now reach your doorstep in minutes, about as quickly as a loaf of bread, with the code ready to redeem the moment it arrives. Blinkit co-founder Albinder Dhindsa announced the offering on X on November 18, noting that it had taken 13 years for the game to arrive. It is a very 2026 way to launch a game, and an apt one, given that Grand Theft Auto has always found its way to Indian players through whichever door happened to be open.

The game itself costs ₹5,999 for the Standard Edition and ₹7,499 for the Ultimate Edition on both PlayStation and Xbox, which is almost exactly double what Grand Theft Auto V cost here at launch. In dollars, though, Indian buyers pay about US$63 for the Standard Edition versus the $79.99 charged in the United States, and pre-order customers also receive the Vintage Vice City Pack. It is on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S only for now, with no PC version announced, which is a shift for a series so many Indians first met on a computer, though Grand Theft Auto V took the same route and reached PC in 2015.

GTA 6 is now live on Blinkit! 🎮 It took 13 years for GTA 6 to be released. In the meantime, we built Blinkit so that you can get the game delivered in minutes. We've launched it in select areas of Delhi, Gurugram, Faridabad, Ghaziabad, Noida, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Mumbai, Pune, Kolkata & Ahmedabad (launching in more cities between today and tomorrow). We'll deliver a physical box with a download code inside (the box is a nice collectible for your shelf). Get yours now and start downloading so you're ready to play from 19th November. Expecting a suspicious number of sick leaves over the next few days 😮‍💨

In solidarity, consumer electronics brand boAt offered employees an optional day off on November 19, announcing it with the caption Out of office. Into Vice City. In Chennai, interior design firm Inde by ChairsCarte declared a holiday for its staff, interns and freelancers, calling it “just a day off for a game we’ve waited years for”.

For a generation of Indian players, the first port of call was the neighbourhood cyber café. Vice City and San Andreas, which defined the series in the early 2000s, were among the first open worlds many Indians explored, playing on rented computers by the hour, often between rounds of Counter-Strike, long before gaming became a career in India. San Andreas also gave us cheat codes, strings of nonsense such as HESOYAM, which replenished health, armour and cash in one go. For those who grew up typing them, they remain shorthand for nostalgia.

Even Indians who have never owned a copy know the series, thanks to its meme culture. The grey-and-red Wasted screen from GTA V, which appears when a character dies, has spent years slapped onto videos of people and animals spectacularly failing at something. Big Smoke’s exasperated yell at CJ for losing a train in San Andreas became so widely shared that Rockstar later named a GTA V trophy Better Than CJ in its honour. But the longest-running joke was about the wait. As the sequel failed to materialise, “We got X before GTA 6” became the Internet’s way of reacting to anything improbable. India took to it enthusiastically, with electronics retailer Croma fuelling another round when the game was delayed to November 19, 2026.

Your KRA is updated to completing missions and side quests 🎮 https://t.co/x1xSmUIPqU

Grand Theft Auto V arrived in India in September 2013, priced at around ₹3,000 for the PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360. But its second life here began after PUBG Mobile was banned in September 2020. Several of India’s biggest streamers, including Dynamo and MortaL, turned to other games, GTA V among them, and roleplay helped make it a mainstay of Indian livestreaming.

A roleplay server is a fan-run version of GTA V’s online world where players invent characters with names, jobs and backstories, from cab drivers and paramedics to cops and small-time crooks, and inhabit them for hours. Soulcity, launched by S8UL and Velocity Gaming in early 2023, became one of India’s biggest GTA V roleplay servers and helped create a new breed of gaming star. S8UL co-founder Lokesh Jain, better known as 8Bit Goldy, played a character called Rocket Singh on the server. The scene grew big enough for S8UL to sign creators such as Sunny Jha, aka Pitaji Playz, specifically for its GTA roleplay roster.

articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: After a 13-year wait, GTA VI is finally here. Built on an estimated $1.5 billion, the game takes players into Leonida’s crime-filled world. Here’s a closer look

Putting an end to the long waiting period of over 13 years, the Grand Theft Auto (GTA) VI by Rockstar Games went live on Thursday (November 19, 2026) for millions of gamers across the globe, offering a gripping landscape of blazing action sequences and adventure-packed missions. The Rockstar Games’ biggest video game, widely reported to be the most expensive cultural product ever made of around $1.5 billion, has released on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X and S. The plot is set in Leonida (a Florida-inspired city), buzzing with traffic, crime and sun-drenched beaches, pairing spectacular visuals with the rise of two small-time criminals through the city’s underworld.

The central characters are a criminal couple, Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, whose action-packed adventures punctuated by slow-motion effects and dramatic camera shifts is expected to the highlight of the videogame. Lucia has recently been released from prison, while Jason is a former soldier who became involved with drug runners in the Leonida Keys. When a criminal job goes wrong, the pair become entangled in a wider conspiracy.
Based on the latest reports, the videogame is not on the cards for the official release in Russia, China, Lebanon or Qatar.

As per the official site, over 4,700 employees cutting across a dozen studios of Rockstar studios, devoted more than eight years to build the latest instalment of GTA. The active production only began after the release of Rockstar’s previous game, Red Dead Redemption II, in 2018. Earlier slated for a late 2025 release , the game’s launch was postponed twice owing to a series of leaks in 2022 and the online release of stolen gameplay videos.

Developers immersed themselves in the region while building the game, driving through Miami, the Florida Keys and surrounding communities, flying over the Everglades and researching the area’s history and architecture.

In a bid to cater to the immersive gameplay experience, the videogame allows players to tune into more than 20 radio stations at home or in their vehicles, with music ranging from Simple Minds and Daft Punk to Van Halen. A fresh addition in the latest instalment is podcasts. Among the options is a true-crime-style series chronicling Vice City, the game’s main metropolis.

The videogame’s plot unfolds by building the relationship between Jason and Lucia, from a chance encounter during a police stop to a robbery gone wrong that lands Lucia in jail. Much of the adventure transpires through lengthy cinematic cut-scenes, allowing players to sit back and watch the story. Only later does the game open up and hand players control of Jason’s day-to-day life, a former soldier working for local gangsters, who is recovering drug packages dropped at sea, stealing cars and shaking down debtors.

The videogame’s release has sparked a wave of excitement among gamers for detailed attention to the graphics. In GTA VI, the hair sways in the wind, muscles flex beneath clothing and characters move with a naturalism. The fictional state of Leonida, Rockstar’s take on Florida, enables a larger-than-life experience to the gamers. This is enveloped by bustling city streets, neon-soaked nightlife and pristine beaches all feature in a vast 3D world that players can explore while scuba diving.

Further, the game’s map is learnt to be one of the biggest and busiest ever made in the GTA-series history. The latest addition allows the non-player characters go about their own lives, and the world seems to carry on whether the player is involved or not. A simple drive across town might involve a random police traffic stop, witnessing a car accident or stumbling across a robbery by the beach.

Additionally, players are likely to find cars heavier in the latest instalment of the video-game, relatably tough to manoeuvre with a responsibility to keep an eye on their fuel tanks. They also decide what stays in a car trunk and what comes along for the ride, juggle phone calls and messages, and use apps to identify targets or track potential scores.

articles.title: IIIT-H students develop web plugin to translate text into Indian Sign Language
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The tool is a simple plugin that lets you select text on a web page, producing a 3D avatar that signs in the Indian Sign Language

The Indian Sign Language (ISL) uses gestures to represent complex words and sentences and has its own grammar and word order. People with hearing impairments find it a challenge to read content online. To address this gap, Masthan Sharif Shaik and Mohammed Raza, third-year BTech. students from the Center for Visual Information Technology (CVIT), IIIT-Hyderabad, under the supervision of Prof. C.V. Jawahar and Prof. Vinay Namboodiri (University of Bath, U.K.), developed a cost-effective plugin that can be added to any website.

The plugin can run inside a browser in real time, without any real hardware or an AI model running on a server. “Websites today support captions, screen readers, and high-contrast modes, but almost none of them can show content in sign language. fullParagraphs: The WHO’s Global Tuberculosis Report 2026 has withheld India’s 2025 incidence estimate pending an assessment of new surveillance data. What does the report reveal about India’s TB burden, and why has the country missed its target?

The story so far: India continues to account for nearly a quarter of the world’s tuberculosis (TB) burden despite expanded diagnosis and treatment services, falling short of the national target of eliminating TB by 2025. According to the World Health Organization’s (WHO) Global Tuberculosis Report, released on November 12, 2026, an estimated 10.6 million people developed TB worldwide in 2025.

While India’s estimated TB mortality rate fell by 38%, from 28 deaths per lakh population in 2015 to 18 per lakh in 2025, the country diagnosed and notified 25.3 lakh cases during the year. However, the WHO has not published India’s estimated incidence for that year, as the figures are under review.

articles.title: GTA VI: Gamers enter Vice City as most-awaited game is rolled out globally
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Game unlocked at midnight on November 19 in each market; Rockstar says story follows criminal couple Lucia Caminos and Jason Duval in Vice City
The wait is over. ‌After 13 years and an estimated $1 billion or more in production costs, the most anticipated video game release in history is finally ​here.

“Grand Theft Auto VI” became available as midnight struck in New Zealand on Thursday (November 19, 2026), with the launch then following the clock around ⁠the world. Millions of players have already downloaded the game to their consoles in anticipation.

The release, with events worldwide and many users taking days off work to play, marks the latest instalment in one of entertainment’s most successful franchises. Since its 1997 debut, “Grand Theft Auto” has become one of the best-selling video game series of all time.

“I’ve been waiting 13 years to ‌play,” said 20-year-old Jonah Bowen-Brown from Australia’s southern island of Tasmania, who persuaded his mother to give him and his brother a week off work at the family-run fragrance shop, Whiff-it!.
“She was really against it at first,” said Bowen-Brown. “I had to say, mum, please, please, I need ‌it.”
A gamer plays Grand Theft Auto VI in Miami, Florida | Photo Credit: Reuters
The game is made by Take-Two Interactive’s Rockstar Games and available on Sony’s PlayStation 5 and Microsoft’s Xbox Series X and S consoles.

The original “Grand Theft ‌Auto” ⁠looks basic by today’s standards, and its missions — stealing cars and carrying out jobs for crime syndicates — angered politicians and parents. But it delighted ⁠gamers.

Each successive release delivered more sophisticated graphics and storytelling. “Grand Theft Auto V”, released in 2013 and set in the fictional Los Santos, a stand-in for Los Angeles, became one of the best-selling video games ever.
While retaining the series’ trademark mix of crime, driving and morally dubious missions, it added activities ranging from parachute jumps to cinema visits and radio stations satirising US culture.

articles.title: Cyclone 'Akvan' LIVE updates: Over one lakh evacuated in Odisha as landfall likely near Gopalpur; red alert for three A.P. districts
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The IMD says the corridor for landfall, likely on Nov. 20 noon, stretches from Andhra's Narsapur in Andhra Pradesh to Odisha's Puri

The Odisha government has set up 9,299 shelters, evacuated over one lakh people to safety, deployed 305 emergency response teams and closed educational institutes in several districts as it has stepped up precautionary measures in view of Cyclone ‘Akvan’, which is likely to cross between Gopalpur and Puri on Friday (November 20, 2026), Chief Secretary Anu Garg said.
The State government is making all-encompassing preparations to tackle the cyclone’s impact, with priority being given to ensure “zero casualties”, she said.
As a precautionary measure, the chief secretary said, “Altogether 1,05,304 people have so far been evacuated, and this process is going on. They have been moved to 1,224 cyclone and flood shelters.”
Altogether 45,364 people have been evacuated in Ganjam, and 18,000 in Gajapati, she said.
Severe cyclonic storm ‘Akvan’ continues to move northwards with a speed of 17 kmph, the IMD said in its latest update on Thursday afternoon (November 19, 2026).

It is likely to move north-northwestward and cross North Andhra Pradesh & Yanam and South Odisha coasts between Narsapur and Puri, close to Gopalpur, by noon of 20th November, 2026 with the maximum sustained wind speed of 90-100 kmph gusting to 110 kmph, it added.

The Srikakulam and Vizianagaram district administrations are on high alert ahead of Cyclone Akvan, which is expected to cross the coast near Gopalpur in Odisha on Friday (November 20, 2026). Srikakulam, which suffered heavily in the two recent cyclones, Arnab and Murasu , is ready to face the new challenge.

Srikakulam Collector Swapnil Dinakar Pundkar and other officials visited Donkuru and other villages of Ichchapuram , on the Andhra Pradesh-Odisha border, to review the preparedness of local officials. Ichchapuram, Sompeta and other areas were badly affected by floods in the Bahuda after the earlier cyclones.

Vizianagaram Collector S. Ramsundar Reddy reviewed the situation at the coastal villages of Pusapatirega and Bhogapuram and asked officials to take necessary measures ahead of the cyclone. He said fishermen had been advised not to venture into the sea for the next few days on the government’s orders.
The IMD on Thursday (November 19, 2026) forecast heavy rain in the southern districts of West Bengal in the next two days as cyclonic storm ‘Akvan’ approaches the east coast.

articles.title: Yadgir ZP CEO directs officials to ensure effective implementation of schemes
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Newly appointed Chief Executive Officer Jubin Mohapatra chairs his maiden meeting with district-level officers of various departments

Chairing a maiden meeting with the district level officers of various government departments, the newly appointed Chief Executive Officer of the Yadgir Zilla Panchayat Jubin Mohapatra has directed them to take concrete steps for the effective implementation of departmental schemes and ensure that funds are utilised within the stipulated timeframe without allowing them to lapse.
Mr. Mohapatra, who assumed charge as the CEO on Tuesday (November 17, 2026), chaired a review meeting in Zilla Panchayat’s VC Hall on Wednesday (November 18).
He stressed the need for timely and target-oriented expenditure of grants released under various Zilla Panchayat heads and other State government programmes.

Emphasising the effective rollout of the State government’s five guarantee schemes apart from the sixth ‘Bhoo Guarantee’ initiative, the CEO instructed officials to ensure that the benefits of every beneficiary-oriented scheme reach eligible people without delay.
He cautioned officers against any irregularities and directed them to discharge their duties responsibly in strict adherence to government guidelines and directives.

Calling for close inter-departmental coordination, Mr. Mohapatra asked officials to keep updated progress reports of all schemes ready at all times and bring any operational issues to his immediate notice.

Announcing a citizen-centric measure, the CEO said a dedicated public grievance redressal cell would soon be opened at the Zilla Panchayat office to address public issues promptly. He urged officials to focus on resolving grievances in a fair and lawful manner.
In-charge Deputy Secretary of the Zilla Panchayat Sharanabasav and various district-level officers attended the meeting.

articles.title: Govt. revises PUC certificate validity, extends renewal intervals for newer BS-VI vehicles
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Private BS-VI vehicles older than 10 years must have their Pollution Under Control (PUC) certificates renewed every six months

The government has revised the validity periods of Pollution Under Control (PUC) certificates, allowing newer BS-VI-compliant vehicles to go longer between renewals while retaining shorter validity periods for older vehicles.

Under the new rules notified by the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways on November 13, BS-VI compliant private vehicles up to six years old will require a PUC certificate once every three years, while those aged more than six years but up to 10 years will need annual renewal.
Government amends rules for vehicle Pollution Under Control certificates. https://t.co/xYX4sMab7g
Private BS-VI vehicles older than 10 years must have their certificates renewed every six months.

The revised schedule also provides longer validity periods for BS-VI-compliant transport vehicles. Those up to six years old will require renewal once every two years, while vehicles aged more than six years but up to 10 years will need annual renewal.
Transport vehicles older than 10 years will continue to require renewal every six months.
For vehicles complying with BS-I, BS-II, and BS-III emission norms, PUC certificates will be valid for three months, while those complying with BS-IV norms will be valid for six months.
The changes have been notified through the Central Motor Vehicles (Sixteenth Amendment) Rules, 2026, under the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, and came into force upon publication in the Official Gazette.

The amended rules also clarify the effective date of renewed certificates. If renewal is sought within the 10 days preceding the certificate's expiry, the renewed certificate will take effect from the expiry date of the existing one. In all other cases where renewal is sought after expiry, the new certificate will take effect from the renewal date.
For certificates issued before the amended rules take effect, the revised validity schedule will apply only when they are first renewed after the new rules come into force.

articles.title: Unions oppose privatisation of Visakhapatnam Port Hospital, plan protest on November 20
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Prime land worth around ₹350 crore is being offered to a private firm for ₹9 crore, the unions allege
All-party trade unions representing workers at the Visakhapatnam Port have strongly opposed the port management’s proposal to privatise the Visakhapatnam Port Hospital.

Demanding the immediate withdrawal of the move and the cancellation of tenders scheduled to be opened on November 21, the unions announced a one-hour protest at the start of duty hours on Friday (November 20, 2026).

Addressing a press conference at the Jagadamba office in Visakhapatnam on Thursday, leaders of the Port All-Party Trade Unions termed the decision to hand over the hospital to private entities an “extremely irresponsible act” that jeopardises the healthcare security of nearly 40,000 port workers, employees, pensioners and their family members.

The union leaders questioned the rationale behind privatising the facility when the Visakhapatnam Port possesses assets worth thousands of crores of rupees, valuable land, its own buildings and substantial reserve funds, while generating annual profits running into hundreds of crores. Calling it shameful for a profit-making port authority to claim it cannot independently upgrade its own hospital, they demanded that the management clarify its intentions to the public.

Raising serious allegations over the terms of the proposal, the unions expressed concern that prime land abutting the National Highway—estimated to be worth around ₹350 crore—is being proposed for handover to a private firm for a mere ₹9 crore. They questioned why the port, despite earning hundreds of crores in annual revenue, could not spend roughly ₹50 crore of its own funds to equip the hospital with modern medical facilities.

Warning that private operators work for profit rather than public service, the leaders said that privatisation would make medical care expensive and impose a severe financial burden on serving employees, retired staff and their dependents. Sacrificing the healthcare security of more than 40,000 dependent families for the commercial interests of private firms was unacceptable, they added.

Instead of pursuing privatisation, the unions demanded that the port management fulfil its social responsibility by upgrading the facility into a full-fledged super-speciality hospital using its own funds, recruiting specialist doctors and medical staff, and procuring state-of-the-art medical equipment and technology.

Prime land worth around ₹350 crore is being offered to a private firm for ₹9 crore, the unions allege

All-party trade unions representing workers at the Visakhapatnam Port have strongly opposed the port management’s proposal to privatise the Visakhapatnam Port Hospital.

Demanding the immediate withdrawal of the move and the cancellation of tenders scheduled to be opened on November 21, the unions announced a one-hour protest at the start of duty hours on Friday (November 20, 2026).

Addressing a press conference at the Jagadamba office in Visakhapatnam on Thursday, leaders of the Port All-Party Trade Unions termed the decision to hand over the hospital to private entities an “extremely irresponsible act” that jeopardises the healthcare security of nearly 40,000 port workers, employees, pensioners and their family members.

The union leaders questioned the rationale behind privatising the facility when the Visakhapatnam Port possesses assets worth thousands of crores of rupees, valuable land, its own buildings and substantial reserve funds, while generating annual profits running into hundreds of crores. Calling it shameful for a profit-making port authority to claim it cannot independently upgrade its own hospital, they demanded that the management clarify its intentions to the public.

Raising serious allegations over the terms of the proposal, the unions expressed concern that prime land abutting the National Highway—estimated to be worth around ₹350 crore—is being proposed for handover to a private firm for a mere ₹9 crore. They questioned why the port, despite earning hundreds of crores in annual revenue, could not spend roughly ₹50 crore of its own funds to equip the hospital with modern medical facilities.

Warning that private operators work for profit rather than public service, the leaders said that privatisation would make medical care expensive and impose a severe financial burden on serving employees, retired staff and their dependents. Sacrificing the healthcare security of more than 40,000 dependent families for the commercial interests of private firms was unacceptable, they added.

Instead of pursuing privatisation, the unions demanded that the port management fulfil its social responsibility by upgrading the facility into a full-fledged super-speciality hospital using its own funds, recruiting specialist doctors and medical staff, and procuring state-of-the-art medical equipment and technology.

Visakha Harbour and Port Workers Union (AITUC) secretary Y.S. Prakasa Rao, Visakha Port Employees Union (HMS) leader S. Arjuna Rao, United Port and Dock Employees Union (CITU) leader V.S. articles.title: OPEC share in India’s crude imports drops to 27.4% in Apr-Oct amid West Asia flare-ups
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: During the mentioned period, India’s crude oil imports spurred about 2.7% to 146.6 million metric tonnes (MMT)

The Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries’ (OPEC) share in India’s crude oil basket declined sharply to 27.4% during April-October of the current fiscal, against 38.5% in the corresponding period last year, according to the latest provisional data released by the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC).

The decline potentially reflects a shift in India’s crude procurement strategy as the country navigates shipping disruptions and geopolitical uncertainties arising from the continuing conflict in West Asia.
During the seven-month period, India’s crude oil imports increased 2.7% to 146.6 million metric tonnes (MMT).
Without identifying individual countries, PPAC data showed that supplies from the Eurasian region accounted for 43.8% of India’s crude oil import basket, while the Middle East contributed 36%.
South America accounted for 10.6% of imports, followed by Africa at 6.6% and North America at 3%.
The changing sourcing pattern indicates a growing diversification of India’s crude oil procurement, with supplies from outside the traditional Middle Eastern market gaining a larger share.

On the petroleum products trade front, diesel accounted for the largest share of India’s exports at 43.4% during the reported period. Petrol and aviation turbine fuel (ATF) followed with shares of 22.4% and 10%, respectively.
On the import side, liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) constituted the largest component, accounting for 50.5% of total petroleum product imports, followed by petroleum coke (petcoke) at 18.3%.
Petroleum product exports remain an important component of India’s external energy trade to contain the impact on its net oil and gas import bill.
Further, PPAC data released on Wednesday showed that petroleum product export volumes declined 13.5% year-on-year during April-October, even as their export value increased approximately 47%.

articles.title: OMCs achieve 0.08% biodiesel blending in H1, lower than target; cite feedstock shortage
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: In the fiscal year 2025-26, OMCs had achieved an overall biodiesel blending of 0.18%

India’s three state-owned oil marketing companies (OMCs) – Indian Oil Corporation, Hindustan Petroleum Corporation and Bharat Petroleum Corporation – achieved an overall biodiesel blending of just 0.08% in the first half of FY27, “significantly below” the indicative target of 5% by 2030, citing limited feedstock availability.
Biodiesel is produced from various feedstocks, including non-edible vegetable oils, animal fat and recycled cooking oil.

Between April and September 2026, the three OMCs sold approximately 4,900 crore litres of diesel. Of this, more than 4,700 crore litres were sold without any biodiesel blending. The remaining 200 crore litres comprised diesel blended with approximately four crore litres of biodiesel, translating into an average blending rate of 2% in the blended portion, they said in a joint statement.
Consequently, biodiesel accounted for 0.08% of the total diesel sold by the OMCs during the six-month period.
The performance also marks a decline from FY26, when the three companies achieved an overall biodiesel blending rate of 0.18%.

The OMCs reiterated that biodiesel-blended diesel conforms to Bureau of Indian Standards specification BIS 1460, which prescribes requirements for automotive diesel fuel, and is covered under the publicly notified National Policy on Biofuels.

They also pointed out that biodiesel blending is an established global practice, with countries such as Indonesia, Malaysia and Brazil adopting blending levels ranging from 10% to 50%, depending on feedstock availability.

fullParagraphs: Hamas denounced a "blatant ceasefire violation," while the military said the rare ground incursion was a response to Hamas ceasefire violations in the area
Israel's military said that a ground operation involving tanks in central Gaza that began the previous day despite a U.S.-brokered ceasefire had come to an end on Thursday (November 19, 2026).

articles.title: COP31 negotiators publish revised deal draft with no mention of fossil fuels
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The revised deal, ‌which is not expected to be the final version, was weaker on some of the conference's central topics — fossil fuels, electrification and adaptation finance — compared to a first draft ‌published on November 16

The latest iteration of the COP 31 draft cover text has eliminated references to fossil fuel phase-out and net-zero dates but has also deleted references to a firm $120 billion adaptation-finance target that developing countries have been asking for as “legally binding financial obligations” on developed countries. This suggests that the most ambitious demands of both the developed and developing country blocs have been eliminated.

A cover text is an overarching political decision that frames the outcome of a climate conference rather than settling any single agenda item. It is usually finalised last, and like every outcome it needs the consensus of all Parties. The Presidency has said earlier drafts were not meant to reflect consensus.

The COP31 Presidency’s revised draft cover decision, dated November 19, has 80 paragraphs, down from 144 in the November 16 version. The summit officially ends on November 20, though negotiations frequently overshoot into the weekend.

A major concern raised by developing countries, of phasing out unilateral trade measures such as the CBAM (Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism) by 2027, that was present in the earlier draft has also been eliminated.

However, a widely expected outcome of raising electricity’s share in final energy consumption to 35% by 2035, scaling up the use of carbon capture utilisation technologies and making early warning systems universal by 2027, continue to find mention in the text. A broad commitment to triple adaptation finance also remains.

“ The draft cover text weaves the 35% electricity in final energy consumption by 2035, alongside tripling renewable energy capacity and doubling the rate of energy efficiency improvement by 2030, ” Ajay Mathur, India’s lead negotiator at Paris COP and former DG, International Solar Alliance, said in a statement. The electricity use in India went up by 13% in 2025 due to the Hormuz crisis alone. It will be an ambitious goal for India to achieve 35% electrification by 2035, but due to the increasing amount of renewable energy in the Indian energy mix, we will be near the 32-34% mark by 2035. ”

“We’re down to the wire at COP31, and the latest texts are alarmingly far from ambitious or equitable,” said Rachel Cleetus, Climate Program director at the Union of Concerned Scientists (UCS) in a statement. “Rich nations, most notably the EU nations, are still holding a harsh line against committing to tripling adaptation finance to at least $120 billion annually by 2035. Instead of reaching agreement on urgently needed climate finance, some countries seem willing to push negotiations toward failure.”

articles.title: Third Ukrainian strike in 4 days halts rail traffic on Russia's Kerch Bridge to Crimea
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The attack came hours before the start of talks in Berlin between U.S. envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy alongside more than 40 European leaders who are supporting Ukraine's war effort

A third Ukrainian aerial attack in four days on the key Kerch Bridge linking Russia to Russian-held Crimea halted rail traffic across the span, officials said Thursday (November 19, 2026), after earlier strikes shut down the road section of the landmark that is a symbol of Moscow's invasion.
Train traffic across the bridge stopped after the overnight strike while authorities assessed the damage, but it resumed in the afternoon, according to Russian state news agency RIA Novosti .

The Ukrainian strikes seemed calculated to embarrass Russian President Vladimir Putin as he met in China with President Xi Jinping and U.S. President Donald Trump, as well as to demonstrate that Kyiv still holds cards in the war and to undermine Russia's argument that its victory is inevitable.

The attack came hours before the start of talks in Berlin between U.S. envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy alongside more than 40 European leaders who are supporting Ukraine's war effort and fear being sidelined by Mr. Trump's direct talks with Mr. Putin.

articles.title: Japanese PM Takaichi says Russia, Japan will keep talking as ties remain chilled
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The last bilateral in-person talks between Japanese and Russian leaders were held between then-Prime Minister Shinzo Abe and Putin in September 2019, during the Eastern Economic Forum in the Russian city of Vladivostok.

Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said on Thursday (November 19, 2026) that she and Russian President Vladimir Putin held talks and agreed to keep communicating in the first such encounter between the two countries' leaders in seven years.

Speaking to reporters on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit, she said she raised the issue of Moscow's treatment of Japanese businesses in Russia and urged Putin to release a Japanese journalist detained for alleged spying during their meeting late Wednesday (November 18, 2026) in Shenzhen, China.
“We reached an agreement to maintain communication at various levels, including direct contact between the president and myself,” Ms. Takaichi said.
Japan's ties with Russia have long been strained by a territorial dispute dating back decades.

Japan lodged a protest with Russia in October over the arrest of a Japanese journalist working for the Hokkaido Shimbun newspaper on suspicion of spying, demanding that Moscow provide an explanation, consular access and humane treatment.

Moscow recently seized control of some local subsidiaries of Japan Tobacco, the largest cigarette maker in Russia, and the company reported it expects a 724 billion yen ($4.5 billion) loss for this year due to the takeover.

Earlier, Japan Tobacco had forecast a 662 billion yen profit for the financial year ending December 31. The company said it has not given up legal ownership of the Russia-based subsidiaries or withdrawn from operating in Russia.

Tensions rose in August after Mr. Putin visited Iturup, one of four Russian-controlled islands off Japan's northern coast that Tokyo also claims. Earlier this month, Tokyo protested after two Russian aircraft briefly violated Japanese airspace off southwestern Japan.

The last bilateral in-person talks between Japanese and Russian leaders were held between then-Prime Minister Shinzo Abe and Mr. Putin in September 2019, during the Eastern Economic Forum in the Russian city of Vladivostok.

Mr. Putin is attending the annual APEC summit for the first time in nine years. He, Chinese President Xi Jinping and U.S. President Donald Trump held a summit meeting on Thursday (November 19, 2026) after the APEC gathering, an event that seems to underscore Japan's diminished role as a global power.

articles.title: Riyadh's tallest building damaged as Saudi reports new Houthi attacks
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The Iran-backed Houthis have stepped up their attacks against Saudi Arabia in recent weeks, striking targets including airports, energy infrastructure, military sites and Riyadh's financial district

A skyscraper in Riyadh housing the headquarters of Saudi Arabia's sovereign wealth fund was damaged on Thursday (November 19, 2026), witnesses told AFP , as the kingdom reported new attacks by Yemen's Houthis.
Saudi Arabia has been battling a surge in attacks since fighting reignited in neighbouring Yemen's civil war, where Riyadh backs the internationally recognised government against the Houthis.
In the early hours of Thursday (November 19, 2026), AFP journalists in the Saudi capital reported a powerful blast was heard.
Around the same time, civil defence authorities issued a warning for "potential danger" but said minutes later that the danger had passed.
The Saudi-led military coalition fighting the Houthis said it had "addressed a missile threat launched by the terrorist Houthi militia towards Riyadh".
"Initial assessment indicates the impact of debris, with material damage currently being surveyed," said coalition spokesman Turki al-Malki.
Witnesses later told AFP that Riyadh's Public Investment Fund Tower, which at 80 storeys is the tallest in the city, had been damaged.
"The facade is damaged across several floors, with windows blown out," said one person who requested anonymity.
"The damage also affected some of the buildings surrounding PIF tower, causing the glass facades on some to shatter. Some of the buildings are residential," the witness added.
Two other witnesses confirmed the damage to the tower, which AFP was unable to visit.

articles.title: Why data interoperability is critical to the future of hospital care
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The future of critical care will be defined by how effectively the information is connected, interpreted and applied

In an intensive care unit, every second matters. A critically ill patient may be connected to several devices, including patient monitors, ventilators and infusion pumps, while laboratory systems and electronic health records continuously generate additional information. Together, these systems create a large and rapidly-changing picture of the patient’s condition. However, when the information remains fragmented across devices and platforms, clinicians may spend valuable time locating, verifying and reconciling data before they can act.

This makes interoperability a clinical priority in critical care, not simply an information technology requirement. Integration enables systems to exchange data, but true interoperability ensures that the information being exchanged is accurate, interpretable and clinically relevant. This can help care teams coordinate and prioritise interventions more effectively while reducing the need to move between multiple systems to assemble a clinical picture.

articles.title: How U.S. controls flow of advanced tech, chip, and compute to China | Explained
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The U.S. Commerce Department, on November 16, 2026, issued an interim final rule barring data centre operators outside of the U.S., equipped with advanced American AI chips, from providing cloud service to businesses in two dozen countries, including China, Iran and Russia

The story so far: The battle for the most sought after commodity that underpins development of artificial intelligence technology just grew fiercer after the U.S. Commerce Department, on November 16, 2026, issued an interim final rule (IFR) barring data centre operators outside of the U.S., equipped with advanced American AI chips, from providing cloud service to businesses in two dozen countries, including China, Iran and Russia. The new, yet to be published, rule also restricts American companies from freely shipping high-end AI chips to a set of five countries, including Indonesia, Malaysia, and Singapore, without the explicit approval of the U.S. government.

China has censured the move, calling it “yet another case of the U.S. overstretching the concept of national security, and abusing export control measures to interfere in normal trade and tech cooperation between China and other countries and go after China’s high-tech industry.”
The interim rule came just days ahead of the meeting between U.S. President Donald Trump and China’s President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen, China on the sidelines of the November 18-19 APEC Summit.

The U.S. government’s policy on making advanced technology inaccessible to China has been a talking point among lawmakers in Washington for well over a decade, but a legal tool to control the flow took shape only during the first Trump term when the administration passed the Export Control Reform Act in 2018.

It gave the U.S. a legal weapon to control the movement of advanced technology originating from the country. Its primary purpose was to curb export of top-tier chips that had dual-use — both commercial and military purposes — to countries like China, Russia and Iran.

Imagine having a medicine that could help manage your child’s rare genetic condition, but being unable to afford it because a year’s treatment costs as much as ₹9 crore. For seven families in India, that situation could soon change.

Seven children diagnosed with Allan-Herndon-Dudley syndrome (AHDS), a rare genetic disorder, are set to receive a year’s supply of the medicine tiratricol free of cost on November 30, following an initiative led by Hyderabad-based paediatrician Dr. Sivaranjani Santosh and Access to Medicines India.

The development is significant not just because the families will receive the medicine without paying for it, but also because its cost has been brought down through pharmaceutical compounding in the Netherlands. While the commercial version of the drug costs approximately ₹4.68 crore to ₹9 crore per child annually, the compounded formulation is estimated to cost just ₹2.5 lakh per child for a year.

The medicine has been prepared by Transvaal Pharmacy in The Hague, Netherlands, with support from the Netherlands-based Pharmaceutical Accountability Foundation (PAF). The first batch will be handed over to the parents of the seven children along with the necessary documentation and individual import permissions. The families have secured approvals for one year of treatment. As the compounded medicine has a shelf life of six months, it will be imported in two batches.

The initiative began after Arav, a child under the care of Dr. Sivaranjani, was diagnosed with AHDS, also known as MCT8 deficiency. The condition is caused by mutations affecting the MCT8 gene, which plays an important role in transporting thyroid hormones into brain cells. Tiratricol, also known as TRIAC, acts on thyroid hormone receptors and may help overcome some effects of the deficiency. It also helps minimise complications associated with peripheral thyrotoxicosis.

Although the medicine was available in Europe, its commercial price put it beyond the reach of most Indian families. Arav’s mother, Pavitra Sirolkar, had to arrange approximately ₹12 lakh to ₹13 lakh for just one month’s supply of the medicine from Germany. Dr. Sivaranjani initially approached paediatricians, endocrinologists and paediatric neurologists to explore ways of procuring the drug. Doctors at Christian Medical College (CMC), Vellore, where five other children with the same condition had been identified, were also approached.

Attempts to obtain the medicine through pharmaceutical company Egetis Therapeutics and its compassionate-use programme did not succeed. The situation eventually prompted Dr. Sivaranjani to take the issue to social media. On September 7, she posted an appeal seeking help for the family and urged people to tag the Prime Minister, Union Health Minister and other government representatives. The appeal gained attention, bringing it to the notice of PAF.

The foundation subsequently explored the possibility of preparing the medicine through pharmaceutical compounding using the active pharmaceutical ingredient. Transvaal Pharmacy conducted test batches and developed a formulation for the seven children. The initial group included Arav and five children receiving treatment at CMC Vellore. A seventh child, aged one year, was identified after his father contacted Dr Sivaranjani following her social media appeal.

According to PAF, the total cost of providing one year’s treatment to all seven children is €14,200, approximately ₹15.08 lakh. Of this, Dr Sivaranjani raised approximately ₹6.09 lakh in India, while PAF undertook to raise the remaining €8,600, approximately ₹9.13 lakh, in the Netherlands. The medicine will be provided to all seven families free of cost.

While the November 30 handover addresses the immediate treatment requirements of the seven children, Dr. Sivaranjani believes that importing the medicine cannot be a permanent solution. She plans to approach the Union government and work with Access to Medicines India and other organisations to explore the possibility of getting the medicine compounded in India and making it accessible to more children.

articles.title: GTA VI generates record $1.1 billion pre-order revenue
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: With record pre-orders and broad market reach, GTA VI is positioned to dominate digital engagement through the end of the year

As Grand Theft Auto (GTA) VI officially launches today , November 19, 2026, a market intelligence report from Sensor Tower highlights an unprecedented shift in consumer engagement and industry revenue.

According to Sensor Tower’s report, the title generated $1.1 billion in pre-order revenue globally across PlayStation and Xbox consoles prior to release, with 11.3 million copies sold. This accomplishment marks the largest pre-launch revenue total on record.

The analytics firms project that total sales could reach $3.2 billion by the end of 2026. Beyond financial performance, the report forecasts a noticeable reallocation of consumer attention across the broader digital landscape.
Daily active user metrics across competing games and entertainment platforms are expected to see a measurable decline as players engage with the new release.
Sensor Tower estimates the average GTA VI player age at approximately 34 years old. This audience displays high companion engagement on second-screen platforms, including Discord, TikTok, and Twitch.
With record pre-orders and broad market reach, GTA VI is positioned to dominate digital engagement through the end of the year.

articles.title: India’s health services has banned reuse of single-use medical devices. But who decides what’s safe?
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Unsafe reuse can harm patients, and billing for a reused device as if it were new is indefensible. But there is a bigger question that needs answering: who decides whether a device can be safely reprocessed, and on what evidence?

I was at Asan Medical Center in Seoul, watching liver transplants at one of the best programmes in the world, just as my own transplant career was beginning. The surgeon fired an expensive surgical stapler, finished the job and threw the device away. I was astonished.

Back home in India, we often used the same stapler again and again, until we felt it was no longer safe. It was so expensive that our patients could afford it only if the cost was shared among many of them.

That memory came back when the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) issued its directive of October 16, 2026 that bans the reuse of devices labelled for single use in all public and private healthcare facilities. The concerns it cites include the risk of infection, possible breaches of existing laws, and cases where patients or government schemes were reportedly charged the full price for reused devices.

These are fair concerns. Unsafe reuse can harm patients, and billing for a reused device as if it were new is indefensible. But there is a bigger question: who decides whether a device can be safely reprocessed, and on what evidence?

Think about rockets. For decades, they were thrown away after a single flight. Then Elon Musk’s SpaceX built boosters that could land, be checked and fly again, and spaceflight became much cheaper. If rockets can be reused, why not medical devices?

In two 2018 Heart Asia editorials, Thomas Crawford, Kim Eagle and colleagues point out that the single-use label is usually decided by the manufacturer, not by an independent regulator who has checked whether it could be safely reused.

A manufacturer that sells a single-use device earns money from every new purchase. Testing a device for reuse is expensive, and the single-use label avoids that cost. Every device thrown away is also a new sale. That said, manufacturers often have good reasons to limit use. Many devices have narrow tubes, fine hinges and delicate coatings that are hard to clean and check properly.

The truth about device reuse in India is not flattering. For years, hospitals have reprocessed devices without consistent protocols, proper tracking or any systematic record of outcomes. Our record on pricing is just as troubling. In 2017, Maharashtra’s Food and Drug Administration reportedly investigated eight private hospitals over the reuse of 1,306 catheters across more than 1,000 patients. Reports also said patients were charged a large part of the maximum retail price for reused balloon catheters.

Reprocessing is more than sterilising. A device can be sterile and still be weakened, unreliable or contaminated in ways the cleaning method does not reach. Depending on the device and the rules that apply to it, a reprocessor has to show that cleaning and sterilisation work, that the device still performs as it should, and that the whole process meets quality and reporting standards.

In the United States, the Food and Drug Administration treats anyone who reprocesses a single-use device as a manufacturer, with the same regulatory duties. Canada, Japan and the European Union have also set up rules for reprocessing, although the details differ from country to country.

This meant that the electorate in those 13 States, that had shrunk from 49.61 crore to 45.22 crore after the SIR, has now gone up to 45.96 crore. The ECI has extended the SSR to States and UTs in Phase 3. As before, it requires no proof of citizenship or mapping to older rolls, and insists on personal notice before any deletion other than of the dead. It also directs Electoral Registration Officers (EROs) to cross-verify deletions personally wherever they exceed 2% of a polling station’s electors. Electors who did not return their forms can do so now, explaining the delay, and those who moved within the State can return through the enumeration form with proof of their new address. itemListElement.headline: After strong El Niño, La Niña may boost India’s 2027 monsoon, says INCOIS forecast
itemListElement.description: Scientists indicate that the ongoing strong El Niño could persist until March 2027, followed by neutral conditions and a possible transition to La Niña during the Southwest Monsoon. They are also monitoring widespread marine heatwaves across the Indian Ocean
